contributions.rationale: Directly establishes that Esrra loss produces a detectable oxidative-metabolism transcript decrease in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
Directly contrasts the Esrra response with flat ESRR paralog and PGC/PPAR-neighbor perturbations in the same responder group.
Supports Esrra specificity by independently showing Esrra alone among ERR-axis comparators generated a resolved 86-gene response in the matched surface.
Supports the non-interchangeability boundary by showing Esrrg comparators, including Esrra and Ppargc1a, do not phenocopy Esrrg.
Further qualifies the claim by showing Ppargc1a, Esrra, and Esrrg do not phenocopy Nrf1 at the single-perturbation level.
Qualifies the network interpretation by showing Ppargc1a is flat while Nrf1 and Esrra are active, indicating pathway divergence rather than a shared PGC-1alpha target set.

higher_order_basis: ERR/PGC/NRF mitochondrial-network members are tested against each other; Esrra uniquely yields an oxidative-metabolism response in the 151 group, while related factors are flat or divergent.
scope: ERR/PGC/PPAR/NRF mitochondrial transcriptional-network perturbations in juvenile neuronal nuclei, especially 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
statement: ERR/PGC/NRF mitochondrial-network membership is not functionally interchangeable in this neuronal assay; Esrra uniquely drives a detectable 151 TH oxidative-metabolism transcriptional signature while Ppargc1a, Esrrb, Esrrg, PPAR targets, and Nrf1-related comparisons are flat or divergent.

contributions.rationale: Anchors the claim by showing represented spinocerebellar ataxia-family targets diverged from Atxn2, with Atxn1 and Atxn10 responding but sharing little of the Atxn2 signature and Atxn7 flat.
Supports the claim by showing related ataxia and polyglutamine-family targets did not phenocopy Atxn7 loss despite some producing FDR-significant genes in matched groups.

Supports and qualifies the claim by showing represented ataxia-family genes were not Camta1 phenocopies and that the Camta1 posterior module should not be treated as a generic ataxia or cerebellar-degeneration signature.

higher_order_basis: The three findings all reject shared acute postnatal neuronal LoF transcriptomic programs based solely on ataxia/polyglutamine disease-family membership, while distinguishing Atxn2, Atxn7, Atxn1/Atxn10, and Camta1-associated modules.
scope: Represented ataxia and polyglutamine-associated perturbations in matched postmitotic neuronal cell groups.
statement: Ataxia or polyglutamine-family membership does not predict a shared acute neuronal loss-of-function transcriptomic state in this screen.

contributions.rationale: Supports extension from structural subunits to an assembly factor and qualifies that lack of transcriptomic overlap does not prove biochemical non-overlap.
Independently anchors the same absence of a convergent complex-I module around Ndufb10, with sparse downstream DE and near-zero score correlations.
Directly anchors the absence of a shared Ndufb7-centered complex-I transcriptional stress module across 21 NDUF structural and assembly-factor comparators.
Supports the broader proposition by showing represented complex-I subunits and assembly factors did not phenocopy Ndufb8 or one another.
Supports the proposition by placing Ndufv1 among flat or sparse Complex-I relatives, while qualifying the interpretation as assay-context buffering rather than functional redundancy.

Supports pathway-level buffering by showing Timmdc1-matched complex-I assembly and structural perturbations were broadly silent, while qualifying that several canonical MCIA genes were not represented.

higher_order_basis: Multiple independent NDUF subunit, assembly-factor, and Timmdc1-centered comparator analyses all report sparse or absent cross-perturbation convergence among represented Complex-I perturbations in the postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq assay.
scope: Represented Complex-I structural and assembly-factor perturbations in the acute postnatal neuronal CRISPR snRNA-seq assay.
statement: Acute perturbation of represented Complex-I structural or assembly genes does not produce a shared soma-detectable mitochondrial-stress transcriptional module in postnatal neurons.

contributions.rationale: Contrasts Alkbh8 flatness with Elp1/Elp2 ISR/amino-acid program despite membership in the same wobble-U34 modification route.
Anchors same-complex Elp1-Elp2 phenocopy and shared same-direction stress signature, including ATF4/amino-acid-associated genes.
Anchors reciprocal Elp2-centered convergence with Elp1 on the 151 ATF4/amino-acid signature.

higher_order_basis: Elp1 and Elp2 same-complex convergence establishes an Elongator-loss stress program, while Alkbh8 non-response bounds the effect to upstream Elongator rather than the entire wobble-U34 pathway.
scope: Strongest in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, with Elp1 broader than Elp2 across 145 and 155; Elp3-Elp6 were not assayed.
statement: Elp1 and Elp2 loss converge on a same-direction ISR/amino-acid transcriptional program in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons that is not reproduced by Alkbh8 loss.

contributions.rationale: Directly shows Lrp6 and Tcf7l2 converge with Ctnnb1, whereas Lrp5, Gsk3b, Frizzled paralogs, Lgr4, Gpc6, and other catenins do not.
Supports the receptor-layer boundary by showing represented Frizzled and PCP receptors did not phenocopy Fzd6 or form a hidden receptor module.
Qualifies the pattern as receptor-level buffering or thresholding, with Lgr4 and Frizzled targets flat and Lrp5/Lrp6 having only singleton-to-small effects.
Directly shows Lrp6 converges with Ctnnb1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut while receptor-level Wnt relatives are flat.
Supports the branch distinction by showing Ror/Fzd/Ryk receptor perturbations were flat while Ctnnb1 and Lrp6 exposed a β-catenin/Axin2/Lef1-sensitive thalamic response.
Supports the rejection of a pan-Wnt receptor model by contrasting flat receptor perturbations with active downstream Wnt transducers Ctnnb1 and Tcf7l2.

higher_order_basis: Across Wnt receptor and effector perturbations, single receptor-family membership poorly predicts transcriptomic phenocopy, while Lrp6-Ctnnb1-Tcf7l2 relationships expose a detectable β-catenin-linked thalamic branch.
scope: represented Wnt/catenin perturbations, especially 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and related thalamic groups
statement: Postnatal neuronal Wnt transcriptomic responses are branch-specific: Lrp6 aligns with the Ctnnb1/Tcf7l2 β-catenin arm, whereas represented single Frizzled, ROR/RYK, Lrp5, and Lgr4 receptor perturbations are largely buffered or nonconvergent.

contributions.rationale: Supports the lesion-specific threshold interpretation by showing Coa8 failed to induce canonical ISR/OXPHOS stress sentinels recovered after Opa1.
Supports broad uncoupling from expected mitochondrial translation stress by showing Gfm2 lacked the ISR-like program and mtDNA transcript decreases seen after Opa1.
Supports the proposition by showing Ndufs2 loss lacked expected ATF4/ISR and mitochondrial transcript changes despite Opa1 detectability.
Anchors the positive detectable Opa1-driven ATF4/ISR-like amino-acid stress program across specified neuronal groups.
Supports the assay-detectability boundary by contrasting Sod2 flatness with Opa1-induced ISR-like genes in the same cell groups.
Anchors the contrast that Sucla2 did not activate the same sentinels while Opa1 did in the same analysis universe.

higher_order_basis: A strong Opa1-positive ISR-like module is repeatedly used as an internal positive benchmark, while several distinct mitochondrial perturbations fail to induce the same nuclear stress sentinels, establishing lesion-specific rather than generic mitochondrial stress transcription.
scope: Mitochondrial perturbations measured in the supplied postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq assay, especially the Opa1-responsive cell groups.
statement: Opa1 loss activates a detectable ATF4/mitochondrial-ISR-like neuronal program that is absent after Sucla2, Ndufs2, Sod2, Coa8, and Gfm2 perturbations in the same assay universe.

contributions.rationale: Reciprocally shows Clock is the closest positive Bmal1 neighbor, sharing same-direction Nr1d2/Dbp-centered features but with a sparser response.
Contrasts Bmal2 flatness with active Bmal1, Clock, Cry2, Nr1d1, and Rora clock-output responses, separating Bmal2 from the detected positive-limb circuitry.
Qualifies the module by showing sleep-related Btbd9 loss is uncoupled from readily detected clock-gene programs in this endpoint assay.
Shows Bmal1 is the strongest positive Clock neighbor and reproduces Clock FDR entries, establishing measurable CLOCK:BMAL1 clock-output convergence.
Qualifies the clock-output module by showing Syncrip does not share stable core clock transcription-factor output despite known phase-dependent clock-related biology.

higher_order_basis: The neighborhood contains reciprocal Bmal1/Clock convergence on clock-output genes, plus multiple non-phenocopy boundaries showing that related or sleep-associated targets do not reproduce that stable endpoint program.
scope: Stable endpoint neuronal clock-output signatures in the supplied clock-related perturbation neighborhood.
statement: The detectable stable neuronal clock-output transcriptional program is centered on Bmal1-Clock convergence, while Bmal2, Syncrip, and Btbd9 do not phenocopy that endpoint program.

contributions.rationale: Anchors that H3K4 writer perturbations produced many detectable downstream calls while Kdm5b eraser perturbation was silent, establishing axis-level asymmetry.
Supports the claim by showing Kmt2a did not phenocopy represented H3K4 writer relatives, with Setd1a broad and Kmt2c nearly flat.
Anchors that H3K4 and REST/PHD-finger comparators failed to phenocopy Phf21a, with some writer and Sin3a perturbations responding differently.

higher_order_basis: All findings examine chromatin regulators connected to H3K4 or adjacent REST/PHD/Sin3a biology and show that detectability and downstream signatures differ sharply by target rather than following a simple shared axis or family phenocopy.
scope: Postnatal neuronal perturbation comparisons among represented H3K4 writers, Kdm5b, Phf21a, REST/PHD-finger comparators, Kdm6b, and Sin3a; missing KDM1A/RCOR/HDAC and several MLL-family subunits limit complex-level inference.
statement: Perturbations of represented H3K4-axis and related chromatin regulators produce target-specific neuronal transcriptomic outcomes rather than a shared H3K4-family or REST/PHD-finger loss-of-function signature.

contributions.rationale: Supports absence of a compensatory or shared nAChR-subunit RNA program around Chrna2.
Supports absence of a family-wide basal nAChR transcriptional module among measurable indirect relatives.
Qualifies the claim by showing a Chrna4-specific one-gene thalamic response that is not reproduced by Chrnb2 or other relatives.
Supports and qualifies the receptor-context interpretation by showing no shared overlap with same-complex alpha6-beta2-beta3 or alpha6-alpha4-beta2-beta3 relatives.
Anchors lack of convergence between Chrnb2 and literature-obvious nAChR relatives, including co-assembly partners.
Anchors lack of phenocopy among alpha6-beta2-beta3 receptor relatives across broad neuronal groups.

higher_order_basis: All findings describe absent shared-direction overlap, near-flat comparator surfaces, or isolated non-overlapping singleton responses across nicotinic acetylcholine receptor subunit perturbations.
scope: represented nicotinic acetylcholine receptor subunit and Ache perturbations in basal postmitotic neuronal snRNA-seq
statement: Single-subunit nicotinic acetylcholine receptor perturbations do not produce a shared basal nuclear transcriptomic state among represented receptor-family members in this assay.

contributions.rationale: Anchors the broad off-panel proposition by showing canonical GPR126-cAMP-PKA-Schwann-myelin effectors were explicitly tested and absent in neurons.
Supports and qualifies the disease-model boundary by showing the peripheral myelin gene module relevant to EGR2-linked neuropathy was not engaged in the neuronal assay.
Supports the claim by showing the canonical MYRF oligodendrocyte myelin-gene program was absent from all sampled neuronal groups.
Supports the claim by showing Nkx6-2 loss did not mobilize oligodendrocyte or myelin maturation markers in sampled neurons.
Anchors the lineage/readout boundary by showing expected Sox10 myelin and neural-crest targets were absent with FDR=1 in the neuronal Sox10 surface.

higher_order_basis: Multiple perturbations of myelin, Schwann-cell, oligodendrocyte, and neural-crest regulators converge on absence of their canonical marker programs in NeuN-enriched neuronal nuclei, localizing rather than falsifying the known biology.
scope: NeuN-enriched juvenile neuronal perturbation surfaces for Adgrg6, Sox10, Myrf, Nkx6-2, and Egr2-related myelin programs.
statement: Canonical glial, Schwann-cell, and myelin transcriptional programs are off-panel in the sampled neuronal perturbation assay.

contributions.rationale: Supports the claim by showing Bckdhb, Bckdk, and Dld collapse to a shared null despite pathway proximity.
Directly states that Bckdk perturbation lacks BCAA-catabolic feedback, ATF4/ISR induction, and mTOR-complex transcriptional feedback across neuronal groups.
Supports and bounds the Bckdk null by showing neither data-driven neighbors nor BCAA/mTOR comparators reveal a hidden Bckdk-like amino-acid-stress signature.
Directly states that Ivd and represented BCAA/leucine-catabolic or ETF-adjacent comparators all have zero downstream significant genes in matched neuronal groups.
Extends the shared buffering pattern to represented organic-acid catabolic comparators while qualifying that these are pathway-neighborhood rather than same-complex MMA comparators.

higher_order_basis: BCAA, leucine, ETF-adjacent, and organic-acid catabolic perturbations repeatedly show matched downstream-null surfaces and lack ISR/mTOR/BCAA feedback signatures in postnatal neurons.
scope: Represented mitochondrial branched-chain amino-acid, leucine, ETF-adjacent, and organic-acid catabolic targets in postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq.
statement: Basal postnatal neuronal perturbation of represented BCAA and related organic-acid catabolic nodes is transcriptionally buffered rather than converted into a detectable nuclear amino-acid-stress or catabolic-feedback program.

contributions.rationale: Anchors complete transcriptional null behavior of Add1, Add2, Add3, and Ank2, with only sparse Sptan1 activity.
Supports RNA-buffering along the adducin paralog axis and direct null behavior of Add1/Add3 perturbations.
Supports that individual adducin-family targets share downstream-null behavior rather than Add3 being uniquely inactive.
Qualifies that Sptan1 has weak Mtor/Gnpat events separated from a generic actin-spectrin membrane-skeleton response.

higher_order_basis: Adducin-family and neighboring membrane-skeleton findings jointly establish that single subunit perturbations are largely transcriptionally silent or sparse.
scope: Represented adducin, spectrin, ankyrin, and related membrane-skeleton perturbations
statement: Single-gene perturbations of represented adducin and ankyrin/spectrin membrane-skeleton components are largely transcriptionally buffered in postnatal neurons.

contributions.rationale: Qualifies the broader Nav/FHF boundary by showing represented FHF, Nav, and receptor-FGF perturbations did not phenocopy Fgf13 in the matched surface.
Directly reports that Scn1b, other alpha-channel losses, and Fgf13 do not phenocopy Scn1a in responder GABA groups.
Directly reports that Nav alpha-subunit paralogs and beta1 partners do not phenocopy Scn1b across the assay surface.
Supports isoform specificity by showing the one-gene Scn3a Slc4a1ap response is not reproduced by assayed sodium-channel relatives.
Supports isoform specificity by showing Scn8a does not phenocopy represented Nav-family perturbations and has shallow consequences.

higher_order_basis: Multiple sodium-channel alpha, beta, and FHF perturbation contrasts agree that physical or family relationships do not yield a shared acute mRNA response in the assayed neurons.
scope: Transcriptomic phenocopy after acute P16 loss in assayed neuronal snRNA-seq groups; not biochemical channel interaction or electrophysiological interchangeability.
statement: Acute perturbations of represented Nav-channel subunits and intracellular FHF modulators produce isoform-specific or sparse neuronal RNA responses rather than a generic sodium-channel transcriptional module.

contributions.rationale: Directly anchors a selective metabolic/redox shift after Chd4 perturbation without canonical UPR/ISR or autophagy markers.
Provides neighboring chromatin-repression activity in the same broader context, bounding Chd4's response as selective rather than a blanket failure to detect chromatin perturbations.
Supports that Chd4 is transcriptionally active in the same thalamic context where Zkscan1 is silent, including shared candidate genes such as Ddo and Msra being FDR=1.0 after Zkscan1 perturbation.

higher_order_basis: Chd4 perturbation produces a metabolic/redox branch in 151, while Setdb1/Zkscan1 comparisons show adjacent chromatin machinery can be active but the response is not a universal chromatin-repression output.
scope: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut chromatin-repression perturbation comparisons involving Chd4, Setdb1, and Zkscan1.
statement: Chd4 perturbation elicits a selective metabolic/redox adaptation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut rather than a broad stress program or universal chromatin-repression signature.

contributions.rationale: Anchors the Pvalb-specific Abat boundary by showing GABA synthesis, transport, glutaminase, and receptor perturbations do not reproduce Abat-Ppp6r1.
Anchors sparse/self-only behavior across GABA synthesis, vesicular loading, reuptake, and catabolism perturbations.

higher_order_basis: Both findings interrogate represented GABA-axis perturbations and agree that perturbing synthesis, vesicular loading, reuptake, catabolism, or receptors yields no broad shared nuclear RNA program, with Abat's Ppp6r1 singleton defining a target-specific exception.
scope: Represented GABA synthesis, vesicle-loading, reuptake, catabolism, glutaminase, GABA_A, and GABA_B perturbations, especially in GABAergic and Pvalb groups.
statement: Sparse perturbation of represented GABA metabolic, transport, and receptor genes does not elicit a shared robust nuclear RNA program in the assayed neuronal groups.

contributions.rationale: Directly reports that Mib1 is the strongest Dctn1 positive neighbor, with 138 same-direction FDR overlaps and no opposite overlaps across sterol genes.
Qualifies module identity by showing Srebf2 perturbation drives the same cholesterol genes down that Dctn1 drives up, validating SREBF2-target activation rather than generic overlap.
Directly reports that Dctn1 is the strongest positive Mib1 neighbor and that Rab7, Htt, Marchf6, and Tsc2 align in the same sterol genes.
Supports the proposition by showing Mib1 and Dctn1 each up-regulate 32 of 34 Srebf2 sterol features, while Txndc15 is weaker.

higher_order_basis: Reciprocal Mib1-Dctn1 convergence and inverse Srebf2 relationships jointly identify a coherent cholesterol regulon activated by unexpected upstream perturbations.
scope: Neuronal sterol/cholesterol-gene transcriptional module across the listed responsive cell groups; convergence does not specify the biochemical step linking Mib1, Dctn1, or related perturbations.
statement: Mib1 and Dctn1 perturbations converge on activation of a neuronal SREBF2-linked cholesterol regulon.

contributions.rationale: Independently shows peroxisomal transporter/import relatives fail to phenocopy Hsd17b4, broadening the null beyond one enzyme.
Shows represented peroxisome-linked comparators are flat or sparse and do not converge on a Pex14-like state.
Supports the peroxisome-specific claim by showing Pex14, Hsd17b4, Abcd3, and Agps do not phenocopy Pex1, with Agps producing a distinct sterol-like response.
Qualifies the claim by showing peroxisomal comparators do not share the Trim37 signature, separating peroxisome membership from that TRIM-family response.

higher_order_basis: Three peroxisome-centered findings independently report flat, sparse, or disjoint responses among represented peroxisomal targets, with Trim37 adding a boundary against mislabeling a separate TRIM signature as peroxisomal.
scope: Represented peroxisome import, transporter, and metabolism perturbations in neuronal snRNA-seq, with several closest PEX targets absent.
statement: Represented peroxisomal perturbations do not produce a coherent shared acute neuronal RNA module.

contributions.rationale: Most presynaptic vesicle or active-zone comparators lacked broad secondary transcriptional phenotypes and did not converge with Cplx2.
Rab27a relatives in secretory-granule and presynaptic pathways were mostly flat or one-gene responders, failing to reveal a Rab27a-like module.
Canonical release-machinery perturbations failed to phenocopy Stxbp1, marking Stxbp1 as a transcriptionally distinct exception rather than evidence for generic release-machinery flatness.
Most represented presynaptic vesicle-cycle comparators were weak like Sv2a rather than producing broad transcriptional outputs.
Syn1 did not phenocopy Syn2 or broader presynaptic-vesicle comparators, many of which were nearly flat.
Syt2 loss did not induce mRNA compensation across synaptotagmins, SNARE regulators, synapsins, active-zone genes, and vesicle-cycle genes.

higher_order_basis: Multiple presynaptic vesicle, SNARE-regulatory, synapsin, synaptotagmin, and Rab pathway perturbation comparisons converge on weak or absent steady-state RNA responses, while Stxbp1 provides a boundary case with a broad non-generic signature.
scope: Acute single-gene perturbations of represented presynaptic release and vesicle-cycle genes in neuronal snRNA-seq
statement: Most represented presynaptic release and vesicle-cycle genes produce little or no broad downstream neuronal mRNA remodeling under single-gene perturbation.

contributions.rationale: Adds that neuronal Kcnq1/Kcnq2/Kcnq3 outputs do not recover the cardiac Yotiao-KCNQ axis, narrowing interpretation to this brain snRNA context.
Shows Kcnq1 does not converge with Kcnq2/Kcnq3 and that Kv7 paralog outputs are sparse and target-specific.
Shows Kcnq3 does not phenocopy Kcnq2 in Kcnq2-responding classes, reinforcing Kv7-subunit specificity.
Shows Kcnq3 is not phenocopied by Kcnq2 or Kcnq1 despite the expected Kv7-family relationship.

higher_order_basis: Multiple Kv7-family and AKAP9 comparator findings jointly show non-convergence among expected channel-related perturbations despite assay recovery of some target knockdown and sparse downstream effects.
scope: Postnatal neuronal snRNA Perturb-seq across the represented Kcnq/Akap9 perturbations.
statement: Represented Kv7-family channel perturbations do not form a shared postnatal neuronal transcriptional response module in this assay.

contributions.rationale: Anchors assay visibility by showing Crem and Scg2 were detectable after Creb1 or Pde10a perturbation while the expected Drd5 immediate-early and CREB-linked program was absent.
Qualifies that the visible downstream cAMP-related responses were sparse and cell-type-restricted, with near-zero whole-surface similarity to Drd5.
Anchors the compartmentalized positive case: Pde10a produced a Scg2/Crem response only in 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA and was not phenocopied by pathway comparators.
Supports specificity by showing only Pde10a/Pde4b produced a few isolated FDR hits among cyclic-nucleotide comparators, rather than a broad PDE1C-like module.

higher_order_basis: Findings about Drd5 and Pde10a jointly show that some downstream cAMP-linked transcripts were detectable, but only in specific perturbation contexts rather than as a tonic receptor-wide module.
scope: CREB/cAMP-linked readouts including Crem and Scg2 in represented Drd5, Creb1, Pde10a, Pde4b, and related perturbations.
statement: CREB/cAMP-linked transcripts were assay-visible in restricted perturbation contexts, but basal Drd5 loss did not engage that transcriptional program.

contributions.rationale: Anchors that represented leucine/BCAA catabolic comparators were downstream-null across 21 neuronal groups.
Supports that same BCKDH-axis biochemical or regulatory relatives Bckdk and Dld were also flat and uncorrelated with Bckdhb.
Anchors that upstream, downstream, regulatory and electron-transfer nodes in BCAA/leucine catabolism all lacked downstream FDR-supported genes in matched neuronal groups.
Supports that represented organic-acid catabolic comparators were downstream-null, extending the shared buffering beyond one cobalamin-associated target.
Anchors a broader buffered organic-acidemia module involving BCAA/organic-acid neighbors and weak TCA/OXPHOS targets.

higher_order_basis: The findings repeatedly show null or near-null RNA responses across connected BCAA, leucine, propionyl-CoA and organic-acid metabolic perturbations, bounding canonical metabolite-flux pathways as uncoupled from robust nuclear DE in this assay.
scope: Postnatal neuronal perturbations of represented BCAA/leucine, propionyl-CoA, organic-acid and adjacent mitochondrial metabolic targets.
statement: Perturbations of represented mitochondrial amino-acid and organic-acid catabolic nodes are broadly buffered from robust downstream nuclear transcriptional responses in the assayed postnatal neuronal groups.

contributions.rationale: Supports and qualifies the proposition by showing the close Tbx2/Tbx3/Tbx4/Tbx5 subfamily and represented BMP/FGF receptor comparators were flat or one-gene responders, with double-loss caveats.
Directly states that Tbx3 did not phenocopy represented T-box relatives and that Tbr1, not Tbx3/Tbx2-subfamily targets, gave the main cortical T-box response.
Directly reports lack of meaningful Tbx4-like convergence among data-driven neighbors and T-box/FGF relatives across the neuronal space.

higher_order_basis: All three findings test T-box-family or developmentally linked receptor comparators and converge on the absence of shared neuronal transcriptomic phenocopy among represented Tbx2/3/4/5-related perturbations, while preserving limits about untested combinations and weak comparator surfaces.
scope: Represented T-box subfamily, BMP, and FGF receptor perturbations in postnatal neuronal CRISPR transcriptomic readouts.
statement: Represented Tbx2/Tbx3/Tbx4/Tbx5-related developmental gene perturbations do not form an interchangeable shared neuronal transcriptional response in this assay.

contributions.rationale: Directly states that Cd40 and measured core CD40-to-NF-kappaB pathway neighbors share a null response, arguing against tonic pathway activity.
Supports the pathway-coherent null by showing Nfkb1, Rel, Traf3, and Tnfrsf1a are also downstream-null across the Chuk-matched neuronal surface.
Qualifies the broad null by noting Fas has its own profile, but measured TNFR/death/NFkappaB/MAPK neighbors fail to phenocopy it as a reusable death-receptor module.
Supports broad refractoriness by showing measurable TNFR-superfamily and NF-kB-adjacent perturbations do not reveal a hidden RANK-like module.
Directly states that TNFR-family and NF-kappaB-neighbor perturbations are essentially flat across the same neuronal groups, with only isolated micro-signatures.
Supports the absence of convergence among TNFR/TLR/NF-kappaB relatives and shows upstream receptors and nuclear components are mostly silent at baseline.

higher_order_basis: TNFRSF, CD40, RANK, TRAF3, CHUK, and NF-kappaB-adjacent comparisons converge on flat or sparse basal neuronal surfaces, with Fas serving as a limited non-reusable exception rather than a shared pathway module.
scope: Unchallenged postnatal NeuN+ neuronal snRNA-seq for represented TNFRSF, TNFR/TLR, TRAF, MAPK, and NF-kappaB pathway perturbations.
statement: Represented TNFRSF-to-NF-kappaB pathway perturbations are broadly refractory in basal postnatal neurons and do not form a shared immune-receptor transcriptional module.

contributions.rationale: Supports broader receptor/SMAD flatness in unstimulated neurons, reinforcing the neuronal rather than ligand-activated disease-axis context.
Directly states that the BMPR2 pulmonary-hypertension gene family is transcriptionally silent in NeuN-enriched neurons and should not be interpreted as a vascular-cell negative.
Supports neuronal BMP-pathway silence by showing Smad9 and BMP receptor relatives are flat or singleton-only.
Supports the absence of a broad neuronal TGF-beta-superfamily program including Bmpr and Acvr receptors.

higher_order_basis: BMPR2-family disease-gene silence is consistent with broader BMP/TGF-beta receptor and SMAD flatness in the same neuronal assay, while Bmpr2:F005 explicitly bounds the interpretation away from vascular PAH cell types.
scope: NeuN-enriched neuronal nuclei only; not pulmonary endothelial, smooth-muscle, immune, or vascular cells.
statement: BMPR2 pulmonary-hypertension-associated pathway genes are transcriptionally silent in the neuronal assay rather than exposing a neuronal version of the vascular BMPR2 disease axis.

contributions.rationale: Independently places tubulin and cytoskeletal genes on a broader structural-remodeling axis across Pvalb, thalamic, midbrain, and sparse cortical/CNU-HYa components.
Shows that Nefh loss does not induce the same tubulin-paralog mRNA compensation in matched neuronal groups, bounding the module away from neurofilament-loss biology.
Contrasts Tuba1a's distinct tubulin-paralog response with flat or weak cytolinker/intermediate-filament comparators, arguing against a generic cytoskeletal stress signature.
Directly identifies a bidirectional tubulin-paralog module in Pvalb and thalamic neurons, with Tuba1a-centered upregulation contrasted against opposite-direction neighbors.

higher_order_basis: Multiple findings converge on tubulin/cytoskeletal RNA behavior while separating it from neurofilament, plakin, and broader cytolinker perturbations.
scope: Postnatal NeuN+ neuronal snRNA-seq signatures, especially Pvalb and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut contexts represented in the neighborhood.
statement: A distinct neuronal tubulin-paralog transcriptional module is induced by Tuba1a loss and echoed on the Atxn10 structural-remodeling axis, but it is not a generic response to neurofilament, plakin, or cytolinker perturbation.

contributions.rationale: Qualifies the claim by showing partner/substitute mRNAs do not compensate after Add1 loss, leaving post-transcriptional or structural compensation possible.
Shows Add1, Add2, Add3, and Ank2 are flat while Sptan1 is only sparse, indicating weak transcriptional output across related scaffold perturbations.
Supports RNA buffering of the adducin paralog axis and distinguishes it from germline compensation at tissue level.
Shows Add1 and Add2 paralog perturbations share the Add3 null, anchoring single-adducin transcriptional buffering.
Supports the broader scaffold claim by showing ankyrin/spectrin/adducin/L1CAM comparators are flat or minimally active and nonconvergent.
Supports the boundary that structural relatives are not interchangeable and do not form a generic actin-spectrin membrane-skeleton RNA response.

higher_order_basis: All six findings describe null, sparse, or nonconvergent RNA consequences across adducins, ankyrins, spectrins, actin, and L1cam, with explicit caveats that mRNA readouts do not test protein localization, phosphorylation, or scaffold mechanics.
scope: represented adducin/ankyrin/spectrin membrane-skeleton perturbations in postnatal neuronal nuclei
statement: Single-gene perturbations of represented adducin/ankyrin/spectrin membrane-skeleton components do not elicit a shared postnatal neuronal nuclear RNA program.

contributions.rationale: Supports the proposition by showing Zmynd8 was the top positive Kdm5c neighbor and recapitulated 13 same-direction genes in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
Anchors the reciprocal Nsd1-centered convergence with Zmynd8 and Kdm5c in the same-direction FDR-overlap neighborhood.
Qualifies the module as selective rather than generic to related chromatin readers, because Zmynd11 was flat where Zmynd8 and Nsd1 shared upregulated genes.
Anchors the shared thalamic positive module by identifying Kdm5c and Nsd1 as the top Zmynd8 neighbors and linking the signature to ZMYND8/KDM5C and NSD1/H3K36me2 biology.

higher_order_basis: Three same-direction convergence findings jointly place Zmynd8, Kdm5c, and Nsd1 in a shared thalamic transcriptional module, while a related reader perturbation provides a boundary condition.
scope: Thalamic glutamatergic cell groups, especially 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut where specified.
statement: Zmynd8, Kdm5c, and Nsd1 perturbations converge on a shared same-direction thalamic neuronal transcriptional module that is not phenocopied by Zmynd11.

scope: L4-5 IT CTX Glut and L2-3 IT CTX Glut perturbation signatures for Mef2c, Grin2a, and related NMDAR/calcium comparators.
statement: Mef2c and Grin2a perturbations share a restricted cortical activity-linked transcriptional state that is not a generic NMDAR, CaMK, calcineurin, or Syngap1 loss signature.

contributions.rationale: Qualifies interpretation by showing clock perturbation can produce mixed feedback rewiring rather than simple oscillator collapse at a single endpoint.

scope: Single-endpoint P16 neuronal snRNA-seq Perturb-seq clock-related comparisons, not circadian time-course or protein-level oscillator measurements.
statement: Several sleep- or circadian-associated gene losses are transcriptionally uncoupled from broad core-clock output modules in postnatal neuronal nuclei.

statement: The represented innate immune receptor and downstream NF-kappaB/IRF/TAK1 circuitry is not engaged as a coherent basal transcriptional module in the assayed neuronal nuclei.

scope: Juvenile postmitotic neuronal snRNA-seq perturbation screen for represented Fe-S and iron-homeostasis genes.
statement: Represented Fe-S and iron-homeostasis perturbations do not resolve into a coherent shared iron-sulfur or canonical iron-stress nuclear mRNA module in juvenile postmitotic neurons.

scope: P16 neuronal snRNA-seq perturbation readouts for represented endomembrane acidification and lysosomal/vesicular genes
statement: Perturbing represented endomembrane acidification components generally fails to produce a shared robust neuronal nuclear transcriptional module in this screen.

scope: Represented cholinergic receptor, muscle AChR, NMJ-associated, and Wnt-AChR perturbations in matched postnatal brain-neuron groups.

contributions.rationale: Anchors the claim by directly showing Dhdds induces a reproducible ER chaperone and ER-quality-control module centered on Hspa5, Hsp90b1, Sdf2l1, Creld2, Herpud1, Manf, Pdia4, and Pdia6.

scope: Susceptible neuronal groups with Dhdds and Manf perturbation signatures and their ER-load comparator relationships.
statement: Loss of Dhdds and Manf converges on an ER client-handling stress response marked by Hspa5-associated chaperone and ER-quality-control genes in susceptible neurons.

contributions.rationale: Anchors that Sucla2 perturbation does not induce Suclg1 or Suclg2 mRNA across measured neuronal groups.

scope: Suclg1/Sucla2 succinyl-CoA ligase perturbations in measured postnatal neuronal groups
statement: Sucla2-associated buffering in this assay is not explained by a detectable nuclear mRNA switch among succinyl-CoA ligase subunits.

contributions.rationale: Supports the receptor-complex boundary by showing Lingo1 effects are not reproduced by Lingo2, Rtn4r, Ngfr, or Trk-family perturbations.

Anchors the proposition by stating that Nogo-A/S1PR2 plasticity pathway comparators lack a recurrent shared-direction neuronal mRNA response.

scope: Measured Nogo receptor, LINGO, S1PR2, Ngfr, Trk, and p75-related perturbations in uninjured juvenile neuronal nuclei
statement: The measured Nogo/LINGO/S1PR2/p75 receptor neighborhood does not resolve into a shared stable neuronal nuclear transcriptomic module in the uninjured juvenile assay.

scope: Represented basal single-gene perturbations in GPCR-linked PLC/Ca2+/PKC/MAPK, mGluR, serotonin receptor, and postsynaptic scaffold pathways in P16 neuronal snRNA-seq; ligand-evoked signaling, electrophysiology, unrepresented G proteins and paralogs, and structural endpoints are outside scope.
statement: Represented GPCR-linked calcium/PLC and postsynaptic scaffold perturbations are largely silent as basal neuronal transcriptomic modules in this screen.

contributions.rationale: Anchors that the assay recovers a canonical ER-stress/UPR program after Atp2a2 perturbation across several neuronal groups, including Ddit3, Chac1, Xbp1, Herpud1, Hspa5, Asns, and Cars.

scope: Atp2a2 and Vps53 perturbations in juvenile neuronal snRNA-seq stress-response readouts.
statement: Vps53 perturbation does not produce the full neuronal UPR/ISR transcriptional program that is detectable after Atp2a2 perturbation.

statement: Smc1a and Stag2 define a shared 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cohesin-linked transcriptional response that is not reproduced by Stag1, Pds5a, Hdac8, Zfp609, Prr12, or Smchd1 perturbation.

scope: Represented kinesin-1, kinesin-pathway, Miro/TRAK transport, and Atcay-related perturbations in juvenile neuronal snRNA-seq readouts.
statement: Acute perturbation of represented kinesin-1 and motor-adaptor transport genes does not converge on a common soma-detectable neuronal transcriptional injury program in this assay.

statement: Familial migraine and related channelopathy genes do not produce a recurrent postmitotic neuronal loss-of-function transcriptome in this assay, indicating that their shared disease biology is not captured as a common nuclear RNA state.

statement: A subunit-selective mSWI/SNF-associated transcriptional module operates in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons, converging across Smarcc2, Smarce1, Arid1a, and Arid2 but not Smarcc1 or Smarca4.

scope: Represented soluble lysosomal hydrolase, M6P-trafficking, and PSAP-related lysosomal perturbations in acute sparse neuronal CRISPR assays.
statement: Represented lysosomal hydrolase and M6P-pathway perturbations are largely buffered at the acute neuronal mRNA level in this sparse mosaic assay rather than converging on a broad storage-stress transcriptomic module.

scope: Postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq after acute perturbation of represented tubulin, dynactin, and microtubule-associated targets.
statement: Microtubule-related perturbations in this assay produce target-specific transcriptomic outputs rather than a generic microtubule-damage program.

statement: B9d1 uniquely exposes a compact cerebellar GABA transcriptional response among the represented ciliary comparator perturbations, while Iqcb1, Rpgrip1l, Rpgr, and Ttc21b do not phenocopy it.

scope: Represented paternally expressed, PWS-region, PWS/AS-neighboring, and imprinting-related neurobehavioral coding-gene perturbations in juvenile postmitotic neurons.
statement: Acute perturbation of individual represented imprinted or PWS-related coding genes does not recapitulate a shared postmitotic neuronal transcriptomic module.

statement: Represented TGF-beta/BMP/activin receptor-SMAD perturbations do not produce a shared basal neuronal gene-expression module in this assay.

statement: Represented peroxisome-linked perturbations generally fail to elicit a shared acute postnatal neuronal transcriptomic module.

scope: Arl3, Arl2bp, and represented ciliopathy comparator perturbations in postnatal brain-neuron nuclei.

statement: A Cav3.1/Cacna1g perturbation elicits a selective thalamic transcriptional response that is not a generic voltage-gated calcium-channel family or auxiliary-subunit loss signature.

Supports non-interchangeability of alpha7 with beta2-containing nAChRs and cholinesterase perturbation.
Anchors absence of shared basal transcriptomic convergence among beta2-related nicotinic receptor subunits.

higher_order_basis: All findings show nicotinic/cholinergic receptor relatives are flat, singleton, or divergent and fail to create shared downstream RNA signatures despite expected receptor-family or complex relationships.
scope: Basal delayed neuronal transcriptomic readout of represented nicotinic and cholinergic receptor-related single-subunit perturbations.
statement: Single nicotinic acetylcholine receptor subunit loss does not produce a shared basal neuronal transcriptional state among represented cholinergic receptor relatives.

contributions.rationale: Shows Ppp2r5d does not phenocopy Ppm1g in 151 TH and that Ppp2r5d downstream DEGs occur in different glutamatergic groups, rejecting a Ppm1g-Ppp2r5d transcriptional phenocopy.

scope: Ppp2r5d and Ppm1g neuronal perturbation signatures in the supplied PP2A/phosphatase-related neighborhood.
statement: Ppp2r5d-associated neuronal transcriptional effects are sparse and cell-type-restricted and do not constitute a shared Ppm1g-Ppp2r5d mRNA phenocopy in this dataset.

contributions.rationale: Directly anchors that Arx loss produced a sparse but real response restricted to inhibitory-neuron groups, with no robust glutamatergic calls.
Qualifies the claim by contrasting retained Arx GABA response with complete Ebf3 flatness despite literature-related developmental positioning.
Qualifies that the mature GABAergic Arx response is disconnected from a literature-obvious endocrine-network relative.
Supports specificity by showing Arx had a small GABAergic response while Pax4 and Pax6 were flat in the same groups.
Supports that the assay could recover an interneuron homeodomain TF response where Pax6 was flat.

higher_order_basis: The Findings center on the same three GABAergic groups and collectively show that Arx has a small postnatal inhibitory-neuron response while related developmental or endocrine transcription factors are flat there.
scope: 046 CTX-CGE GABA, 052 Pvalb Gaba, and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA in the P16 perturbation assay; Arx, Pax4, Pax6, Ebf3, and Neurog3 comparisons.
statement: Arx loss retains a sparse postnatal GABAergic transcriptional response that is not shared by Pax4, Pax6, Ebf3, or Neurog3 perturbations in the same inhibitory-neuron groups.

contributions.rationale: Anchors lack of convergence between Camk2a and CaMKII paralogs, calmodulins, Dlg4, and AMPAR/NMDAR-related perturbations.

Contrasts transcriptionally quiet PSD/SynGAP scaffold perturbations with active NMDAR subunit perturbations, defining the boundary between receptor subunits and downstream scaffold/CaMKII nodes.

scope: Postmitotic neuronal groups represented for CaMKII, calmodulin, NMDAR, AMPAR, PSD scaffold, and Syngap1 comparisons
statement: Basal neuronal RNA responses distinguish NMDAR subunit perturbations from downstream CaMKII paralog and PSD scaffold perturbations, which do not form a shared Ca2+/CaM-NMDAR/PSD transcriptional module.

scope: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut perturbations involving Braf, Map2k1, Shoc2 and Ntrk2.
statement: A RAF-to-MEK-linked neuronal transcriptional module in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut is marked by shared down-regulation of Vgf with partial overlap on Ptpn5, Unc13a and related genes.

scope: Sampled Ras/FGFR/RAF/MEK pathway perturbations in postnatal neuronal groups, especially 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
statement: The detectable thalamic Braf/Map2k1 transcriptional output is not upstreamed to Kras, Hras, or Fgfr3 loss in this screen.

scope: Postnatal neuronal single-gene perturbations of represented Wnt receptors and downstream Wnt nodes
statement: Most represented single Wnt receptor perturbations are transcriptionally buffered or nonconvergent in postnatal neurons, whereas selected downstream Wnt nodes and Lrp6 can expose detectable thalamic beta-catenin-associated output.

statement: The few FDR-supported neuronal transcriptomic hits observed among represented complex-III-related perturbations are target-private rather than phenocopies of same-complex perturbation.

scope: Baseline postnatal neuronal loss-of-function snRNA readout without ligand challenge
statement: Measured steroid and estrogen nuclear-receptor perturbations do not form a shared basal neuronal transcriptional module, despite occasional receptor-specific signatures.

scope: basal P16 NeuN-positive neuronal groups measured by snRNA-seq
statement: Basal neuronal Adar or Ifih1 loss does not elicit a detectable type-I-interferon/ISG transcriptional program in the measured NeuN-positive neuronal groups.

contributions.rationale: Anchors that represented Frizzled and PCP receptors do not phenocopy Fzd6 or form a hidden receptor module under single-gene P16 neuronal perturbation.

Supports that Ror1, Ror2, Fzd2, Fzd4, Fzd6, and Fzd9 do not converge with Ryk.

scope: Represented Wnt receptor-level perturbations in P16/postnatal neuronal groups, with several unmeasured Wnt ligands and receptor-complex components absent.
statement: Represented single Wnt receptor perturbations are largely transcriptionally buffered and do not form a shared postnatal neuronal receptor-level module.

Qualifies the claim by showing the sparse Smo Rnf220 hit is not a coherent Smo-like or opposite Hedgehog module in 155 MB Glut.

higher_order_basis: Across receptor, ciliary, cAMP, SMO, and GLI perturbations, the findings repeatedly show absence of canonical Gli1/Ptch/Hhip-type reporter movement and no shared pathway phenocopy, with isolated singleton hits treated as boundaries.
scope: P16 NeuN+ neuronal perturbation screen for represented Hedgehog, ciliary, and cAMP pathway components.
statement: The P16 NeuN+ neuronal screen lacked a detectable canonical Hedgehog-GLI transcriptional circuit after acute perturbation of represented pathway components.

contributions.rationale: Supports nonconvergence of RAR/RXR-family perturbations and qualifies that Rara and ligand/combinatorial tests were absent.
Supports partner-specific rather than shared basal RXR network behavior across measured RXR paralogs and partner receptors.

scope: Acute single-gene postmitotic neuronal perturbations of represented retinoid, RXR, VDR, and nuclear receptor partner targets.
statement: Single-node perturbation of represented retinoid/RXR/VDR nuclear-receptor pathway members does not produce a coherent shared acute neuronal transcriptional module in this assay.

scope: Represented phosphorylase-kinase components Phka1 and Phkb, plus Calm1/2/3 comparators, in postnatal neuronal groups assayed by snRNA.
statement: The represented phosphorylase-kinase components Phka1 and Phkb do not define a shared neuronal transcriptional module, and sparse calmodulin paralog responses do not phenocopy that complex.

scope: Represented thyroid receptor/RXR/nuclear receptor perturbations in measured neuronal groups.
statement: The accessible thyroid nuclear-receptor RNA response in this acute neuronal assay is TRα-selective rather than a generic consequence of perturbing Thrb, RXR partners, or related nuclear receptor components.

Directly anchors the absence of convergence between Ndufs2 and 21 represented complex-I subunits or assembly factors.
Supports the interpretation that flat or sparse Complex-I responses reflect assay-context buffering rather than a Ndufv1-specific outlier.

scope: represented Nduf/Ndufaf Complex-I perturbations in the P16 postmitotic neuronal CRISPR transcriptomic assay
statement: Represented nuclear Complex-I subunit and assembly-factor perturbations fail to produce a shared acute neuronal OXPHOS-stress transcriptomic module in this assay.

Shows Dnm1 is flat while Cltc and Stxbp1 are responsive, bounding the claim to transcriptomic effects rather than vesicle physiology.

statement: Represented clathrin/endosomal and synaptic-vesicle genes do not form a single shared neuronal transcriptomic module; Cltc-associated responses are separable from buffered adaptor, APP-risk, and vesicle-recycling perturbations.

Supports absence of a shared Xylt1-like GAG module among B3gat3, Ext1, and Ext2, with near-zero correlations.
