Supports pathway-level absence by showing literature-obvious receptors and SMADs failed to phenocopy a broad neuronal program.

scope: Represented activin/BMP/TGF-beta receptors and SMAD perturbations in postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq contexts, not phospho-SMAD activity; several pathway members were untested.
statement: Basal postnatal neurons in this screen lack a detectable shared activin/BMP/TGF-beta receptor-to-SMAD transcriptional program.

statement: Basal neuronal bHLH-PAS perturbations split into an active CLOCK/BMAL1 circadian transcriptional module and a largely flat ARNT/AHR/HIF/NPAS branch.

statement: Acute neuronal perturbation signatures among represented PHF/PHD-domain and H3K4-associated chromatin regulators are target-specific rather than explained by generic family membership or a uniform failure to detect chromatin-regulator loss.

Qualifies the scope by showing same-pathway and upstream nodes did not phenocopy Mtor loss, while noting protein-level effects may be missed.
Contrasts buffered receptor-proximal PI3Kβ with detectable downstream Tsc2 and weak Mtor transcriptional signatures.
Supports the same upstream PI3K buffering by showing Pik3r2 and Pik3cb were as transcriptionally buffered as Pik3r1.
Supports the proposition across receptor/proximal PI3K relatives, with Pik3r1, Pik3cb, Akt3, Igf1r, Insr, Rptor, Erbb3, Erbb4, and Mapk1 flat in matched groups.

higher_order_basis: Multiple findings independently report flat or near-zero transcriptional responses for receptor-proximal PI3K/AKT/mTOR relatives, while downstream Tsc2 remains detectable and Mtor itself is separated from same-pathway phenocopy.
scope: Basal sparse postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq perturbation surfaces represented in this neighborhood.
statement: Single perturbation of receptor-proximal PI3K/AKT and related mTORC1-adjacent nodes is transcriptionally buffered in basal postnatal neuronal nuclei, whereas downstream Tsc2 can produce a detectable mTOR-axis RNA phenotype.

contributions.rationale: Supports the claim by showing AKAP/PKA comparators lack an Akap11-like transcriptional module, with only Gsk3b showing a small divergent response.
Anchors broad buffering across represented AKAP-family and cAMP/PKA-pathway perturbations.
Qualifies the broad buffering by identifying Gsk3b as a narrow exception rather than a pathway-wide transcriptomic response.
Independently anchors buffering of PKA holoenzyme core and AKAP localization nodes at downstream RNA level.

higher_order_basis: Akap9, Prkar1a, and Akap11 comparisons all report absence of shared downstream RNA programs across AKAP and PKA-related perturbations, with Gsk3b only adding a restricted exception.
scope: represented AKAP/cAMP/PKA/GSK3β perturbations in postnatal neuronal nuclei
statement: Single-gene disruption of represented AKAP localizers and PKA core nodes is generally buffered at the basal nuclear RNA level in this assay.

contributions.rationale: Anchors robust Pura specificity by showing Purb had zero exact FDR overlaps with Pura-responsive genes and Purg was completely flat.
Supports the claim by showing Purb did not phenocopy PUR paralogs or nearby RNP-granule comparators and had only a private one-gene signature.
Anchors the complementary contrast that Pura produced many downstream FDR genes whereas Purg produced none and was orthogonal to Pura.

higher_order_basis: All three findings compare PUR-family perturbations in matched postnatal neuronal groups and consistently show robust Pura-specific transcriptional output with Purb weak/private and Purg absent.
scope: PUR-repeat family perturbations in acute postnatal neuronal Perturb-seq
statement: PUR-repeat paralogs are not transcriptionally interchangeable in P16 neurons, with robust neuronal mRNA consequences localized to Pura loss rather than generic PUR-family depletion.

contributions.rationale: Directly states that primary-cilium, BBSome, IFT, and ciliary-GPCR targets did not phenocopy Alms1 and were flat or singleton at the DE level.
Qualifies the broader ciliary claim by showing ARL3's expected ciliary relatives were orthogonal or flat, while noting unassayed ARL3-cycle perturbation targets.
Supports the claim by separating ciliary trafficking from nuclear expression output, with ciliary GPCR, IFT, and Hedgehog components producing singleton or zero downstream signatures.
Directly states that IFT, transition-zone, BBSome, and Rfx3 comparators were null or singleton responders and did not converge into Hedgehog or ciliary-GPCR expression programs.
Supports that represented IFT, dynein-2, BBSome, and transition-zone perturbations were transcriptionally buffered in Kif3b-matched groups.
Supports rejection of a hidden BBSome/IFT mRNA phenotype through near-orthogonal and zero-or-one-gene comparator surfaces.

higher_order_basis: Six independent ciliary-neighborhood findings report that represented IFT, dynein-2, BBSome, transition-zone, ciliary-GPCR, Hedgehog, and ARL3-related perturbations are flat, singleton, orthogonal, or non-phenocopying in neuronal snRNA readouts.
scope: Postnatal neuronal snRNA perturbation readout of represented ciliary transport, BBSome, transition-zone, ciliary-GPCR, Hedgehog, and ARL3-related targets.
statement: Loss of represented ciliary trafficking and signaling components rarely resolves into a shared basal neuronal mRNA program in this assay.

contributions.rationale: Directly anchors the existence of an aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase induction program after Bdp1 perturbation.
Contrasts and bounds the claim by showing Polr3b did not induce ISR, aminoacyl-tRNA-synthetase, or UPR/ERAD mRNAs despite detectability of those mRNAs in the same analysis layer.

higher_order_basis: One finding establishes a compact Bdp1-associated synthetase induction response, while the other shows that a Pol III catalytic subunit perturbation does not share that mRNA stress response under the same neuronal assay layer.
scope: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut mRNA stress readouts after represented Pol III-related perturbations.
statement: Aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase induction is a Bdp1-associated neuronal mRNA response that is not a general consequence of Polr3b perturbation in this assay.

contributions.rationale: Directly reports limited CHD interchangeability: Chd4 induces Chd3, but Chd2 and Chd8 are distinct and Chd7 is nearly inert.
Directly reports that CHD paralogs, Wnt/beta-catenin targets, BAF components, and other ASD chromatin genes did not phenocopy Chd8.

higher_order_basis: Both findings reject simple phenocopy among represented CHD/chromatin perturbations while preserving narrow evidence for Chd4-associated paralog transcript induction.
scope: P16 neuronal basal snRNA-seq perturbation assay for represented CHD paralogs and ASD/chromatin pathway genes.
statement: Represented CHD paralog and ASD-associated chromatin perturbations were not transcriptionally interchangeable in the P16 neuronal assay.

contributions.rationale: Ctcf loss repressed a broad clustered protocadherin program in thalamic and midbrain neurons.
Setdb1 loss opposed Ctcf on gamma-protocadherin genes, distinguishing repressor and CTCF maintenance arms at the same locus.
Smchd1 had no FDR-level Pcdh calls despite Setdb1 and Ctcf detectability, qualifying Smchd1 as outside the acute Pcdh-maintenance node in this assay.

higher_order_basis: Ctcf and Setdb1 both affect clustered protocadherins with opposite directions, while Smchd1 lacks a detectable Pcdh phenotype in the same assay context.
scope: Clustered protocadherin transcriptional regulation after chromatin-factor perturbation in postnatal neuronal nuclei.
statement: Clustered protocadherin transcription in postnatal neurons is detectably maintained by Ctcf and opposed by Setdb1-dependent repression, whereas Smchd1 is not acutely required for an FDR-level Pcdh expression phenotype in this assay.

contributions.rationale: Supports and contrasts by showing Hspa5, not Atf6, exposes the detectable ER quality-control module in the matched thalamic group.
Supports and contrasts by showing Hspa5 up-regulates ER quality-control genes in the same group while Edem3 does not.
Qualifies by separating a one-gene Nmnat2 overlap from the broader Hspa5 ER-stress signature, which does not accompany Fgf12 loss.
Anchors the positive module by directly stating that Hspa5 perturbation induces ER folding and ERAD genes in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
Supports and qualifies by showing Lman2l does not induce the Hspa5-like UPR/ERAD program, restricting the claim to broad durable UPR output.
Supports by showing Mttp lacks ER-stress/ERAD induction while Hspa5 induces the same marker set in the dataset.

higher_order_basis: One Hspa5-centered positive response repeatedly serves as an internal detectability control for ER folding/ERAD transcripts, while several ERQC, secretory, ATF6, and unrelated perturbations fail to induce that broader program.
scope: ER proteostasis and related perturbations in thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic neurons and matched postnatal neuronal groups.
statement: The postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq assay can detect an Hspa5-driven ER folding/ERAD transcriptional response, but Edem3, Atf6, Lman2l, Mttp, and Fgf12 losses do not broadly activate that durable UPR-like RNA program.

contributions.rationale: Anchors that ABCA7-related Alzheimer's and phagocytic comparator targets were mostly flat in neurons, placing expected biology outside the healthy NeuN-enriched transcriptional axis.
Supports lineage-gated interpretation by showing CSF1R-axis microglial comparators were also flat in the same neuronal readout.
Supports the proposition by showing TAM and phagocytic/microglial relatives did not converge with Mertk in matched neuronal groups.
Anchors that myeloid-lineage Spi1 comparators were flat while neuron-active benchmarks were detectable, arguing against a globally insensitive DE workflow.

higher_order_basis: All findings point to absent or non-convergent neuronal transcriptional responses for Alzheimer's/phagocytic/myeloid genes, while Spi1 includes positive neuronal benchmarks showing detectability of other perturbation classes.
scope: Healthy NeuN-enriched postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq readout across matched brain cell groups.
statement: ABCA7, TAM/phagocytic, and myeloid-lineage perturbations do not expose a shared neuronal transcriptional program in the healthy NeuN-enriched screen.

contributions.rationale: Supports and qualifies the claim by distinguishing ciliary trafficking components from detectable nuclear RNA effects, while noting snRNA-seq may miss receptor localization or cilium-length changes.
Contrasts ciliary-Hedgehog flatness with broad Psmb4/Psmc1 responses, showing the weak ciliary response is not a universal assay insensitivity.
Supports the lack of a common IFT/ciliary Hedgehog module by showing ciliary comparators had near-zero correlations and singleton or absent FDR events.
Anchors pathway-class transcriptional buffering among IFT-B, dynein-2, Cep290, BBSome, and Hedgehog-related perturbations rather than a shared Ift88 knockout transcriptome.
Anchors the absence of a shared NPHP5/CEP290/RPGR/BBSome/IFT neuronal module across 22 matched groups.
Supports absence of a hidden BBSome/IFT mRNA phenotype through non-convergence of same-organelle comparators with Ttc8.

higher_order_basis: Ciliary structural, trafficking, dynein-2, BBSome, GPCR, and Hedgehog-pathway perturbation findings repeatedly report zero or singleton nuclear RNA effects and lack of convergence, with proteasome perturbations showing the assay can detect broad responses.
scope: Postnatal NeuN-positive neuronal groups represented for IFT, BBSome, dynein-2, CEP290/IQCB1, ciliary GPCR, and Hedgehog comparator panels
statement: Perturbation of represented neuronal ciliary trafficking, IFT/BBSome, dynein-2, and Hedgehog-axis genes is poorly coupled to a shared cell-autonomous nuclear RNA response in postnatal NeuN-positive neurons.

contributions.rationale: Supports and qualifies the claim by showing Sec23a and Tfg were flat and essentially uncorrelated with Sar1b across matched neuronal groups, with scope limited to represented COPII relatives.
Anchors convergence between Sec23a and Sar1b on a flat downstream phenotype, supporting shared buffering of the SAR1/SEC23 branch.

Anchors that Tfg, Sec23a, and Sar1b proximal COPII-related perturbations were flat, whereas Sec63 produced an ER-stress response, defining a COPII-buffered branch rather than generic ER perturbation flatness.

higher_order_basis: All three COPII/ER-exit findings independently report flat or near-zero downstream responses among represented Tfg, Sec23a, and Sar1b perturbations, while one finding contrasts this with Sec63 ER-stress positivity.
scope: Represented COPII initiation/ER-exit perturbations in postnatal neuronal groups.
statement: Perturbing individual represented COPII initiation or ER-exit nodes Tfg, Sec23a, and Sar1b is transcriptionally buffered in this neuronal assay, unlike the ER-stress response elicited by Sec63.

contributions.rationale: Supports the pathway-level interpretation by showing alpha-dystroglycan and DGC relatives did not phenocopy Crppa or converge into a shared module.
Qualifies the biological interpretation by warning that the juvenile neuronal null should not be used to infer reversibility of embryonic dystroglycanopathy malformations.
Anchors the claim by showing DGC, dystroglycan-glycosylation, and neurexin relatives failed to phenocopy Dag1 and did not produce a shared dystroglycanopathy module.
Supports the matriglycan/DAG1-glycosylation boundary by showing Large1 did not phenocopy other directly assayed glycosylation or DGC targets.
Supports the claim by showing Sgce did not join a coherent dystrophin/sarcoglycan-complex transcriptomic module.
Anchors the DGC/DAPC null component by showing Dag1, Dmd, and Sgce mirrored Snta1 null while Sgcd had only a sparse exception.

higher_order_basis: DAG1, DGC/DAPC components, and alpha-dystroglycan glycosylation or matriglycan pathway genes were repeatedly flat, sparse, or nonconvergent in the postnatal neuronal transcriptomic assay, with caveats about protein/glycan biology and developmental timing.
scope: Represented dystroglycan, dystrophin-glycoprotein-complex, and alpha-dystroglycan glycosylation perturbations in postnatal neuronal cell groups.
statement: Sparse postnatal neuronal loss of represented dystroglycan/DGC and alpha-dystroglycan glycosylation genes does not generate a shared dystroglycanopathy-like nuclear RNA module in this assay.

contributions.rationale: Ago2, Dicer1, Tnrc6b, and mostly Tnrc6a did not phenocopy Ago1, showing the near-null behavior spans several miRISC nodes.
Dicer1 and represented Ago/TNRC6 effector nodes were flat or nearly flat, anchoring broader miRNA/RISC-axis buffering.
An isolated Dicer1 up-regulation lacked Drosha/Dgcr8/Ago/Xpo5/Tarbp2 support, qualifying isolated miRNA-gene movement as not evidence for a coordinated pathway response.
Other single miRISC core perturbations did not reproduce Tnrc6a's two MB Glut genes, supporting paralog and pathway buffering.

higher_order_basis: Multiple miRNA biogenesis and effector-node comparisons show flat or singleton responses and lack of cross-phenocopy under single-gene perturbation, with isolated Dicer1 movement not expanding to a pathway signature.
scope: Represented miRNA/RISC perturbations in postmitotic neuronal snRNA-seq readouts
statement: Single-gene perturbations of represented miRNA/RISC pathway components are buffered or nonconvergent at the postmitotic neuronal nuclear-RNA endpoint.

contributions.rationale: Directly states that represented core miRNA/RISC relatives did not phenocopy Ago1 and were flat or near-flat in matched groups.
Independently anchors that canonical miRNA/RISC perturbations failed to converge on an Ago2-like response and had near-zero correlations.
Qualifies the scope by showing a Pvalb Tnrc6a-associated hit did not behave like a robust core miRNA-effector loss state.
Supports the proposition by showing other single miRISC core perturbations did not phenocopy Tnrc6a in MB Glut.

higher_order_basis: Several single-node perturbations within Ago/TNRC6/Dicer miRNA effector machinery fail to produce shared downstream transcriptional modules in matched neuronal groups, implying buffering or lack of module-level transcriptional output in this assay.
scope: Represented single-gene miRNA/RISC effector perturbations in postmitotic neuronal cell groups
statement: Single-gene perturbation of represented core miRNA/RISC effector nodes does not produce a coherent shared neuronal transcriptional loss-state in this assay.

contributions.rationale: Supports the claim by contrasting null Hdac8 with overlapping Smc1a and Stag2 thalamic signatures.
Qualifies the claim by showing Pds5a did not phenocopy the restricted Smc1a/Stag2 response, limiting the module to specific cohesin components rather than all cohesin regulators.
Supports the claim by reporting that Smc1a and Stag2 triggered overlapping 151 signatures while Prr12 remained near-null in the same matched comparison.
Anchors the claim by identifying Stag2 as the strongest same-direction Smc1a neighbor in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, with 14 shared genes, while other relatives were flat or divergent.
Qualifies the claim by showing Stag1 did not act as a generic cohesin phenocopy and that Stag2 opposed the Stag1 Gabra1 effect.

higher_order_basis: Multiple matched thalamic comparisons identify Smc1a and Stag2 as the convergent pair, while Stag1, Pds5a, Hdac8, Prr12, and other chromatin-loop or cohesin-linked perturbations fail to phenocopy them.
scope: Represented cohesin and cohesin-linked perturbations in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons.
statement: The postnatal thalamic cohesin-related transcriptional response is selectively shared by Smc1a and Stag2 rather than by represented cohesin regulators or cohesin-linked factors broadly.

contributions.rationale: Supports target-specificity by showing Flt4's 308 CB GABA Tmem129 response was not reproduced by canonical VEGFR3-pathway comparators.
Directly anchors that Kdr's 054 CNU-MGE GABA Clasp1 response was not shared by VEGF/Sema3E relatives or downstream PI3K/MAPK nodes.
Qualifies receptor-complex expectations by showing the near-null Nrp2 surface did not hide a shared Nrp1, Plexin-A, Kdr/Flt4, or Gria state.
Contrasts these private neuronal signatures with the broader uncoupling from vascular targets.

higher_order_basis: Private Kdr and Flt4 neuronal responses are bounded by multiple pathway-comparator failures, showing target-specific hits rather than recovered canonical receptor complexes.
scope: Kdr and Flt4 neuronal signatures relative to represented VEGF/Sema3E/neuropilin and signaling comparators.
statement: The Kdr Clasp1 and Flt4 Tmem129 neuronal responses are target-specific signatures rather than shared VEGF receptor or neuropilin pathway outputs.

contributions.rationale: Anchors the positive Atxn2 response: up-regulation of a small synaptic and neurite-structure module in 151.

Qualifies and bounds the Atxn2 state by showing Yy1 and Psmb4 perturbations regulate the restricted signature in the opposite direction rather than matching a generic chromatin-factor or proteasome-loss injury program.

higher_order_basis: The neighborhood contains one positive Atxn2 module finding and one comparator contrast showing inverse regulation by Yy1/Psmb4 over the same restricted signature, jointly defining the Atxn2 state and its non-generic boundary.
scope: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut Atxn2 perturbation signature
statement: Atxn2 perturbation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut induces a small synaptic/neurite transcriptional state that is distinct from Yy1- or Psmb4-associated inverse injury-like signatures.

contributions.rationale: Supports the claim by showing represented TCA, PDC, and Fe-S neighbors did not phenocopy Aco2 and mostly remained buffered.
Directly anchors that DLD-pathway perturbations across carbon-entry and TCA enzymes were no-DE or singleton/sparse, supporting broader postmitotic buffering.
Directly anchors that mitochondrial pyruvate-entry/PDC neighbors and most TCA or malate-aspartate comparators were null or self-transcript-only.
Qualifies the claim by showing Ogdh had a Prdx5/Borcs7 signature that did not generalize to same-complex or neighboring mitochondrial enzyme perturbations.
Supports the claim by showing PDC comparators and related TCA comparators failed to form a coherent neuronal PDH module.

higher_order_basis: Multiple perturbations spanning mitochondrial pyruvate entry, PDC, DLD-linked complexes, TCA enzymes, and Fe-S neighbors repeatedly show flat, singleton, or non-phenocopy mRNA surfaces, with Ogdh providing a bounded divergent exception.
scope: Represented postmitotic neuronal mitochondrial carbon-entry, PDC, DLD-linked, TCA, and Fe-S enzyme perturbations
statement: Basal postnatal neuronal nuclei show broad transcriptomic buffering to represented mitochondrial carbon-entry and TCA-enzyme perturbations, with only sparse or target-specific exceptions.

contributions.rationale: Anchors the pathway-level near-silence of measurable Gbeta5/R7-adjacent perturbations across matched groups.
Qualifies the claim by showing a receptor-specific lone CA3 event that was not reproduced by GPR158-paralog, RGS7-complex, class-C GPCR, or cAMP-pathway perturbations.
Supports the absence of a substitute Gpr179-like brain module among represented retinal-cascade relatives.
Supports the lack of phenocopying among represented mGluR-family and ON-bipolar signalplex comparators.
Supports and qualifies the claim by showing the Rgs6-associated Pvalb Wdfy3 decrease was not reproduced by Gnb5 or represented GABA_B/GIRK and inhibitory-GPCR perturbations.

higher_order_basis: The findings collectively test Gbeta5/R7-adjacent, GPCR, GIRK, retinal signalplex, mGluR-family, and cAMP-related perturbations and find flat, sparse, or receptor-specific nonconvergent transcriptomic outputs.
scope: represented Gbeta5/R7-adjacent, GPCR, GIRK, mGluR, and retinal signalplex perturbations in postnatal neuronal transcriptomic assays
statement: Represented Gbeta5/R7-adjacent and related GPCR signaling perturbations do not form a shared postnatal neuronal transcriptomic module.

contributions.rationale: Supports the non-generic interpretation because Cplx2 and related release components lack broad convergent RNA phenotypes.
Supports the boundary by showing Stx1b itself has no meaningful presynaptic-pathway neighbor or downstream FDR response.
Anchors that Stxbp1 is not phenocopied by canonical SNARE-cycle and release-machinery perturbations.
Supports the contrast by showing another core fusion perturbation stops at target-transcript loss without secondary remodeling.

higher_order_basis: Stxbp1 is compared against several canonical release-machinery findings that remain transcriptionally sparse or self-limited, defining its signature as non-generic for SNARE-cycle perturbation.
scope: Stxbp1 relative to represented SNARE-cycle and presynaptic release comparators
statement: The Stxbp1 nuclear transcriptomic signature is not a generic consequence of perturbing canonical SNARE-cycle or presynaptic release components.

contributions.rationale: Directly identifies mostly down-regulated adhesion, extracellular-matrix/guidance and excitability genes in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut after Smc1a perturbation.

Independently reports a same-cell thalamic Stag2 signature dominated by down-regulated adhesion, extracellular-matrix, synaptic and neuronal-signaling genes, with overlapping genes including Ptprm, Adamts2, Adamts19, Sema5a, Necab2 and Lrrc7.

higher_order_basis: Both cohesin-related perturbations in the same thalamic neuronal class converge on down-regulation of neuronal adhesion/connectivity and signaling/excitability gene classes, while both caveat that these are transcriptomic gene-set interpretations rather than direct chromatin or electrophysiology measurements.
scope: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons after postnatal Smc1a or Stag2 perturbation
statement: Smc1a and Stag2 loss both depress a thalamic postmitotic neuronal connectivity/signaling transcriptomic module in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons.

contributions.rationale: Anchors that Bmal1 perturbation changes clock-output genes but also up-regulates feedback components, indicating mixed feedback rather than simple oscillator collapse.
Anchors that Clock loss depresses canonical circadian-output genes including Nr1d2, Dbp, Tef, and Per3 across subcortical or pineal-containing bins.
Qualifies the activator/repressor interpretation by showing Cry2 loss moved Dbp and Nr1d1 in the same direction as Bmal1 and Clock loss in 151 TH.
Supports cell-context detectability while narrowing Nr1d2 loss to a limited Nr1d1/Cacna2d3 edge instead of broad clock-output derepression.

higher_order_basis: Clock and Bmal1 perturbations establish detectable clock-output repression and feedback changes, while Cry2 and Nr1d2 constrain the result against a simple linear oscillator model at a single endpoint.
scope: Single-endpoint postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq clock-network perturbations, especially 151 TH and subcortical/pineal-containing bins.
statement: Clock-network perturbations in the assayed neurons produce detectable but context-dependent circadian-output transcriptional changes that are not explained by a simple linear activator-versus-repressor model.

contributions.rationale: Supports the broader calcium-channel/calcineurin branch boundary by showing absent or minimal coordinated RNA footprint across related targets.
Qualifies the calcineurin branch by showing calcineurin-subunit signatures are not simple Nfatc3-loss signatures.
Supports the claim by showing a constitutive calcineurin-to-NFATC3 transcriptional module was not recovered.
Qualifies the claim by identifying Ppp3r1 as a small, specific thalamic program rather than a generic NFAT/FKBP12-like signature.
Anchors the lack of convergence between Ryr2 and ryanodine/IP3/calmodulin/CaMK-signaling relatives.
Anchors the transcriptionally inert RyR/IP3 release-channel neighborhood and lack of CaM/CaMK convergence with Ryr3.

higher_order_basis: The findings jointly show that represented calcium-release channels, calmodulin/CaMK comparators, calcineurin subunits, FKBP12, and NFATC3 do not form a coherent constitutive steady-state RNA module, while narrow calcineurin-subunit effects remain specific.
scope: Represented neuronal calcium-release, calmodulin/CaMK, FKBP12, calcineurin, and NFATC3 perturbations
statement: The represented calcium-release and calcineurin/NFAT pathway perturbations are largely uncoupled from a shared constitutive neuronal steady-state RNA program.

contributions.rationale: Supports and qualifies the claim by showing ETS and endothelial-receptor proxies failed to phenocopy Elf2, with true paralogs absent from the perturbation set.
Directly reports that represented ETS-family and Ras-MAPK/BMP pathway nodes did not phenocopy Ets1, with zero-to-tiny signatures and near-zero correlations.
Directly states that other ETS-family targets did not phenocopy Spi1 in neurons despite shared ETS DNA-binding ancestry.

higher_order_basis: The findings independently test Ets1, Spi1 and Elf2 against available ETS-family and pathway-linked comparators and converge on non-phenocopying, while caveating missing close paralogs and generally weak comparator perturbations.
scope: Represented ETS-family, Ras-MAPK/BMP, and endothelial-receptor-proxy perturbations in neuronal matched-group transcriptomic readouts.
statement: Shared ETS-family membership is insufficient to produce a common neuronal perturbation transcriptomic state among the represented ETS targets in this assay.

contributions.rationale: Contrasts the convergent spliceosome/RNA-processing responders with buffered Ctnnbl1 despite PRP19-complex membership.
Supports the broader RNA/nuclear logistics state by linking Ogt loss to recurrent splicing-transcript downregulation and positive neighbors including Tnpo3, U2af2, and Prpf6.
Directly anchors convergence among spliceosome-process neighbors across strongest midbrain/thalamic responders.
Independently anchors broad RNA-splicing convergence with Rnpc3, Prpf6, Snrnp70, U2af2, Cdc40, and Hnrnpu.
Contrasts direct spliceosome perturbations with Snrpn, which fails to phenocopy them despite being compared in the same assay universe.
Supports and narrows the claim by showing Tnpo3 convergence is with spliceosome/RNA-processing perturbations rather than generic nuclear transport.

higher_order_basis: Strong same-direction convergence among several RNA-splicing and RNA-processing perturbations is repeatedly observed, while Ctnnbl1 and Snrpn define boundaries where RNA-related genes do not behave as core spliceosome-like responders.
scope: Postnatal neuronal gene-level snRNA-seq perturbation signatures in midbrain, thalamic, hypothalamic, and related responder groups represented in this neighborhood.
statement: Core or adjacent RNA-splicing perturbations form a recurrent same-direction neuronal transcriptional response module that is not shared by all RNA-associated genes.

contributions.rationale: Anchors CHD-family non-phenocopy by showing Chd4, Chd7, and Chd8 do not reproduce Chd2 responses in matched responder groups.
Anchors reciprocal divergence by showing Chd8, Chd2, and Chd4 respond where Chd7 is flat with essentially no overlap with Chd7.

higher_order_basis: Both findings independently show divergence among represented CHD-family perturbations in overlapping postnatal neuronal responder groups.
scope: Matched postnatal neuronal responder groups including 151 TH, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA
statement: Represented CHD-family perturbations do not produce interchangeable postnatal neuronal transcriptomic phenotypes, with Chd2-specific responses separated from flat or nonoverlapping Chd7-associated comparisons.

contributions.rationale: Directly reports that Cic is the strongest positive Atxn1 neighbor, with 177 of 256 Atxn1 FDR genes also significant under Cic in the same direction.
Directly reports that Atxn1 is the nearest measured Cic signature neighbor and phenocopies the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c module.

higher_order_basis: The two reciprocal perturbation-centered findings independently identify each gene as the other's strongest positive neighbor in the same neuronal subtype and same-direction module.
scope: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut postmitotic neuronal subtype; convergence is strongest in the responding signature and does not test unrepresented Atxn1l or Etv perturbations.
statement: Cic and Atxn1 loss converge on a shared same-direction 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c neuronal transcriptional module.

contributions.rationale: Anchors the claim by showing canonical SMAD feedback and TGF-beta target transcripts were absent from the Tgfbr1 perturbation surface across all tested groups.
Supports and operationalizes the claim by identifying Smad7, Serpine1, Skil, and ID-family transcripts as poor basal neuronal engagement markers in this perturbation format.

higher_order_basis: Both findings from the same perturbation neighborhood establish that canonical ligand-responsive TGF-beta transcripts remain unchanged after basal neuronal Tgfbr1 CRISPR loss and therefore do not serve as engagement readouts in this context.
scope: Basal P16 neuronal snRNA-seq Tgfbr1 loss-of-function assay across 22 measured cell groups.
statement: Canonical TGF-beta response transcripts do not report basal Tgfbr1 loss-of-function engagement in juvenile neurons under this unstimulated snRNA-seq assay format.

contributions.rationale: Directly anchors that represented IFN receptor and IFN transcription-factor relatives lacked a coherent IFN-stimulated response in matched neuronal groups.
Directly anchors that Stat1 flatness matched a broader unliganded IFN/STAT neighborhood, with no recurrent IFN module across receptor, IRF, NF-kB, ISGF3, and STAT comparators.
Supports the broader cytokine/STAT inactivity context by showing multiple receptor and STAT perturbations were flat or produced non-overlapping singleton effects.

higher_order_basis: Interferon receptor, IRF, and STAT comparator perturbations repeatedly fail to produce an IFN-stimulated transcriptional module under basal conditions.
scope: Basal postnatal neuronal IFN receptor, IRF, and STAT comparator perturbations
statement: The sampled basal neuronal state lacks a coherent IFN-response transcriptional dependency on represented IFN receptor, IRF, and STAT perturbations.

contributions.rationale: Anchors that Becn1 produces downstream genes only in three neuronal groups and is multi-gene only in 155 MB Glut.
Supports by narrowing Becn1 phenocopy to a small subset rather than broad canonical autophagy relatives.
Supports the broader boundary that canonical autophagy and lysosome perturbations do not behave interchangeably with Rb1cc1 across matched responder groups.

higher_order_basis: Cell-type selectivity of Becn1 and cross-autophagy non-phenocopy jointly bound autophagy-related RNA responses to restricted neuronal contexts.
scope: Postnatal NeuN-positive neuronal snRNA responses to represented autophagy perturbations.
statement: Core autophagy-gene perturbations do not elicit pan-neuronal transcriptional responses in this assay; detectable responses are restricted to a small set of neuronal cell groups.

contributions.rationale: Supports that 21 other complex-I Nduf/Ndufaf perturbations produced only 0-3 downstream genes each, pointing to family-wide transcriptional buffering.
Supports that Ndufaf2 did not converge with represented structural or assembly perturbations and that protein-complex membership should not imply a shared transcriptome.
Anchors that represented Complex-I subunits and assembly factors did not phenocopy Ndufb8 or each other, rejecting a shared mitochondrial-stress transcriptome.
Supports that same OXPHOS complex membership, including NDUFB/ND5-module neighborhood, did not translate into shared acute neuronal transcriptomes.
Anchors the same family-level absence with 21 comparators showing near-zero correlations and no FDR overlap with Ndufs2 responder genes.
Supports and qualifies that same-complex relatives were flat or sparse, indicating assay-context buffering rather than proving functional redundancy.

higher_order_basis: Six findings independently describe flat, sparse, non-overlapping, or near-zero-correlated transcriptomic responses across broad Nduf/Ndufaf Complex-I structural and assembly perturbation panels.
scope: Represented nuclear-encoded Complex-I subunit and assembly-factor perturbations in the postnatal neuronal CRISPR/snRNA-seq assay.
statement: Represented Complex-I subunit and assembly-factor perturbations do not generate a shared acute postnatal neuronal OXPHOS-stress transcriptional module.

contributions.rationale: Supports the broader class-level null by showing represented serotonin receptors were flat or singleton responders rather than robust Htr1a phenocopies.
Supports receptor-specific separation by showing measured serotonin-receptor relatives did not reproduce the Htr1f Sst-Zfp513 event.
Qualifies the class-level conclusion with a same-complex boundary: even Htr3a did not phenocopy sparse Htr3b hits, while electrophysiological effects remain untested.
Supports the claim by reporting Htr4 and other single serotonin receptor perturbations, including Gs relatives, did not phenocopy each other.
Qualifies the claim within Gs/cAMP-related receptor biology by showing Htr6 was not reducible to a generic 5-HT4/6/7-Gs-cAMP transcriptional module.
Anchors the proposition by reporting that ten represented Htr-family perturbations produced only 0-2 downstream genes per target and no robust shared basal neuronal DE module.

higher_order_basis: Multiple serotonin receptor perturbation comparisons independently report flat, sparse, or nonoverlapping transcriptional responses rather than a shared basal Htr-family neuronal module, with additional receptor-subfamily and same-complex contrasts bounding the interpretation.
scope: Represented serotonin receptor single-gene perturbations in the unstimulated postnatal snRNA-seq neuronal assay.
statement: Represented serotonin receptor loss does not produce a robust shared basal neuronal transcriptomic module in this assay.

contributions.rationale: Anchors the positive signal: Cacna1g loss produced 14 downstream genes only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
Supports and contrasts the positive Cacna1g 151 response with Cacna2d2 flatness in the same cell group.
Supports the claim by showing most represented CaV relatives were flat or singleton while Cacna1g was the only multi-gene calcium-channel response, restricted to 151.

higher_order_basis: All three findings identify Cacna1g as the only represented calcium-channel perturbation with a multi-gene response, and locate that response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut rather than broadly across channel-related targets or cell groups.
scope: Represented calcium-channel perturbations across matched neuronal groups, especially 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
statement: Cacna1g loss produced a narrow 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut multi-gene transcriptional response that was not shared by represented HVA calcium-channel auxiliary or pore-related perturbations.

contributions.rationale: Qualifies the claim by separating ciliary trafficking and Hedgehog/GPCR axes from nuclear expression readouts in matched neuronal groups.
Supports pathway-level buffering by reporting no meaningful Ift43 signature neighbor and singleton or no FDR events among cilium/Hedgehog comparators.
Directly frames cilium-related perturbations as converging mainly by transcriptional buffering rather than a shared IFT-B knockout transcriptome.
Supports the buffered ciliary-transport module through zero or one downstream gene among IFT, dynein-2, BBSome, and transition-zone comparators.
Adds a ciliary polycystin context where trafficking and assembly perturbations remain nearly flat rather than producing a Pkd1-like response.
Supports the absence of a hidden BBSome/IFT mRNA phenotype by showing ciliary comparators are nearly orthogonal to Ttc8.

higher_order_basis: Across BBSome, IFT, kinesin, dynein-2, transition-zone, ciliary GPCR/Hedgehog, Cep290, and Pkd1 contexts, findings repeatedly report flat or singleton transcriptional responses instead of a robust shared ciliary module.
scope: Postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq perturbation surfaces for represented ciliary transport, BBSome, transition-zone, GPCR/Hedgehog, and Pkd1-related genes; ciliary morphology and protein localization were not measured.
statement: Perturbing represented neuronal ciliary genes is largely buffered at the nuclear mRNA level and does not induce a robust shared ciliary transcriptional program.

contributions.rationale: Anchors orthogonality between Gabra3 and represented GABA_A receptor or inhibitory-synapse relatives across many neuronal groups.
Adds boundary evidence that an adjacent GABA-A receptor subunit and inhibitory-synapse comparators produced only isolated non-overlapping hits rather than a shared module.
Supports by showing gephyrin perturbation did not alter GABA(A), glycine-receptor, or inhibitory-synapse gene transcripts at FDR level.

higher_order_basis: The GABA_A receptor and scaffold comparisons jointly reject a simple inhibitory-synapse transcriptional module while distinguishing transcriptomic readout from synaptic protein physiology.
scope: Represented GABA_A receptor and inhibitory-synapse perturbations
statement: Perturbing represented GABA_A receptor subunits and inhibitory-synapse scaffold genes does not yield an interchangeable inhibitory-synapse transcriptional state in juvenile postmitotic neurons.

contributions.rationale: Supports the claim by showing shared flat or singleton responses across activin/BMP/TGF-beta receptor and SMAD targets.
Anchors the broad BMP receptor/SMAD observation that Bmpr1a and measurable pathway neighbors fail to form a coherent loss-of-function transcriptional module.
Qualifies the claim in the Sst Gaba context by showing that RGM-neogenin/BMP pathway perturbations do not reproduce the Hjv Rxylt1 response.
Supports the claim by showing that neogenin/BMP-axis relatives are sparse or flat and do not phenocopy Rgma.

higher_order_basis: Multiple BMP/TGF-beta/RGM-neogenin pathway perturbations independently show flat, singleton, or nonconvergent neuronal transcriptomic surfaces.
scope: Postnatal unstimulated neuronal snRNA-seq for represented BMP/TGF-beta receptor, SMAD, RGM, and neogenin-axis targets
statement: Represented BMP/TGF-beta receptor, SMAD, and RGM-neogenin perturbations do not produce a coherent shared postnatal neuronal mRNA module.

contributions.rationale: Directly anchors that assayed mGluR-family and retinal signalplex perturbation comparators failed to phenocopy Grm6.
Directly anchors that ON-bipolar cascade readout transcripts did not move after Grm6 perturbation, with all listed cascade tests at FDR 1.0.
Supports by showing group-I and group-III mGluR comparators did not expose hidden pathway-level convergence.
Supports by showing other represented mGluR paralogs were flat, placing Grm6 in a broader receptor-family buffered context.

higher_order_basis: Grm6 loss neither changes canonical ON-bipolar cascade transcripts nor shares a basal brain RNA phenotype with assayed receptor or signalplex comparators.
scope: Basal snRNA-seq largely outside retinal physiological readouts; cannot assay retinal dendritic localization, electroretinogram b-waves, visual behavior, or TRPM1 gating.
statement: Grm6 perturbation does not produce a detectable basal RNA-level ON-bipolar or mGluR-family response in the assayed neuronal nuclei.

contributions.rationale: Anchors lack of convergence between Dpysl5 and semaphorin/plexin/GSK3B/Fyn or microtubule comparators.
Supports that receptor relatives acted on different single genes in different groups rather than a common downstream state.
Supports by showing Plxna4 loss did not transcriptionally regulate assayed co-receptors or intracellular signaling nodes including Rac1, Fyn, Dpysl2, Dpysl5, Cdk5, and Rras.
Qualifies expected biology as wiring, extracellular-matrix, protein, and cytoskeletal mechanisms outside the acute single-nucleus transcriptome.

higher_order_basis: Receptor, intracellular signaling, and microtubule-neighbor findings jointly bound semaphorin-pathway biology as poorly captured by acute nuclear mRNA convergence.
scope: Represented semaphorin/plexin receptors, CRMP, kinase, cytoskeletal, and microtubule comparator perturbations
statement: The assayed semaphorin/plexin pathway does not transmit into a shared acute nuclear mRNA program across represented receptor, CRMP, kinase, and microtubule perturbations.

contributions.rationale: Qualifies the vascular receptor portion by showing canonical VEGFR3-pathway comparators do not phenocopy Flt4 or recover a VEGFR3 module.
Directly states that NRP1 family and pathway neighbors fail to produce a broad Nrp1-like transcriptional phenotype.
Directly states that neuropilin, Plexin-A, VEGF-receptor, and AMPAR comparators fail to phenocopy Nrp2.
Supports the claim by rejecting an interchangeable semaphorin-receptor transcriptional state among plexin, neuropilin, and semaphorin relatives.
Qualifies the vascular-lineage interpretation by showing VEGF/Tie/neuropilin and Rac/Pak vascular comparators are also flat in neurons.
Supports the vascular-lineage boundary by showing Vezf1 neuronal responses are uncoupled from represented VEGF/endothelin vascular targets.

higher_order_basis: Neuropilin, plexin, semaphorin, VEGF/Tie/endothelin, Robo4, and vascular-effector comparisons repeatedly fail to converge in NeuN-enriched postmitotic neurons, bounding these pathways as not recovered as canonical receptor modules in this assay.
scope: Represented neuropilin/plexin/semaphorin and vascular receptor-effector perturbations in the NeuN-enriched neuronal assay
statement: Represented semaphorin-neuropilin-plexin and vascular VEGF/Tie/endothelin/Robo pathway perturbations do not form shared canonical receptor transcriptomic modules in the NeuN-enriched postmitotic neuronal screen.

contributions.rationale: Directly states NK-homeobox or ventral-patterning comparators do not phenocopy the isolated Nkx2-1 Pvalb Med13 hit.
Directly states represented NK-family and prostate-axis perturbations do not uncover an Nkx3-1-like neuronal program.

higher_order_basis: Both NK-homeobox neighborhood findings independently show near-null or isolated responses that fail to converge with represented NK-family comparators in the sampled neuronal groups.
scope: Represented NK-homeobox-related perturbations in Pvalb, CA1/DG, and CA3/CA2-FC/DG neuronal groups.
statement: Represented NK-homeobox perturbations do not define a shared postnatal neuronal transcriptional program in the sampled groups.

contributions.rationale: Contrasts Med13 with its paralog Med13l, showing limited interchangeability outside the shared 151 Grm1 signal.
Directly reports that Med15 and Med23 converge with Med13 on the same 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut down-regulated module.
Qualifies the module by showing only Grm1 is reproducibly shared with Med13l and Cic, while Cdk8 does not share it.
Directly reports shared-direction repression of a 151 thalamic neuronal gene module across Med15, Med13, and Med23 perturbations.
Contrasts the convergent Med13/Med23 relationship with non-phenocopy by Med13l and Cdk8, bounding the module to selected Mediator perturbations.
Supports the claim by identifying Med15 and Med13 as convergent with the Med23 151-thalamic module.

higher_order_basis: Several findings identify an overlapping down-regulated 151 thalamic gene set shared by Med13, Med15, and Med23, while separate comparisons show Med13l and Cdk8 do not broadly phenocopy that program.
scope: Measured Mediator perturbations in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons, with limited reference to 059 and 005 responder contexts where stated.
statement: Med13, Med15, and Med23 perturbations converge on a shared down-regulated 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neuronal module that is not broadly reproduced by Med13l or Cdk8.

contributions.rationale: Supports the claim by showing Rora/Nr1d1-related accessory-loop programs diverge from Clock and that Rorb/Rorc are flat.
Supports non-interchangeability among REV-ERB/ROR and other circadian relatives in the thalamic responder context.
Anchors absence of detectable clock-gene module engagement or convergence after Rorb loss despite circadian behavioral relevance.
Anchors flat Rorc behavior despite active related ROR/REV-ERB/circadian perturbations, especially in the thalamic group.

higher_order_basis: ROR/REV-ERB/accessory-loop findings show activity for some members but flat or divergent surfaces for Rorb/Rorc and weak phenocopy among related circadian targets.
scope: Represented ROR/REV-ERB and related circadian perturbations in postnatal neuronal groups
statement: ROR/REV-ERB family and accessory clock regulators are not transcriptionally interchangeable in the postnatal neuronal assay.

contributions.rationale: Directly states canonical VEGFR3-pathway comparators did not phenocopy Flt4 or regulate the Flt4-associated Tmem129 response.
Directly states measured VEGF/Sema3E relatives and downstream nodes did not phenocopy Kdr or share its Clasp1 response.
Directly states neuropilin, Plexin-A, VEGF-receptor, and AMPAR comparators failed to phenocopy Nrp2.
Supports the broader vascular-pathway boundary by showing Vezf1 neuronal signatures were uncoupled from VEGF/endothelin vascular targets.

higher_order_basis: All findings test represented VEGF/neuropilin/vascular receptor or downstream pathway comparators and consistently reject matched neuronal phenocopy.
scope: Represented VEGF/neuropilin/semaphorin/endothelin vascular-pathway perturbations in NeuN+ postmitotic neuronal CRISPR readouts.
statement: Canonical VEGF/neuropilin vascular-pathway relationships are not recovered as a shared neuronal transcriptomic module in the NeuN+ postmitotic CRISPR assay.

contributions.rationale: Qualifies the claim by showing represented tRNA-modification disease relatives diverge by target, complex, and neuronal context rather than forming one transcriptomic syndrome.
Supports specificity by showing Alkbh8, Nsun2, and Trmt1 fail to reproduce the Elp1/Elp2 TH response.
Anchors the positive Elongator-associated ATF4/integrated-stress-response program in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
Supports assay capability by showing Elp1 and Elp2 converge on ISR/amino-acid signatures while Nsun2 is flat.
Qualifies the claim as a branch separation among represented tRNA methyltransferases rather than a generic tRNA-writer effect.
Anchors that Elp1 and Elp2, but not Trmt1, induce the robust amino-acid/ATF4 ISR module in the same dataset.

higher_order_basis: Across multiple tRNA-modification comparisons, Elp1/Elp2 repeatedly provide the positive ISR/amino-acid transcriptional branch, whereas Nsun2, Alkbh8, Trmt1, and Cdkal1-related comparisons define flat or divergent boundaries.
scope: P16 neuronal snRNA-seq perturbation signatures for represented tRNA-modification and Elongator-related targets in thalamic, midbrain, and related neuronal groups.
statement: In this neuronal screen, Elongator disruption selectively elicits an ATF4/amino-acid integrated-stress transcriptional program that is not a generic consequence of represented tRNA-modification enzyme loss.

contributions.rationale: Anchors the non-phenocopy among Calm paralogs despite identical calmodulin protein sequence.
Anchors the family-level observation that Calm1, Calm2, and Calm3 do not form a shared FDR signature.
Supports the claim by showing Calm3-specific anchor genes are not reproduced by Calm1 or Calm2.
Qualifies the scope by showing Camta1 loss does not alter basal Calm-family or Camta2 mRNA in the measured groups.
Qualifies the broader calcium/phosphorylase-kinase context by showing Phkb is flat while Calm effects remain sparse and cell-restricted.
Qualifies the claim by extending the non-equivalence to an indirect downstream calcineurin comparison.

higher_order_basis: Multiple same-family and pathway-level contrasts show that identical calmodulin-coding loci produce sparse, locus-specific or flat RNA consequences rather than a shared CaM-depletion transcriptional state.
scope: Juvenile postnatal neuronal Perturb-seq assay for Calm-family and related calcium-signaling comparisons
statement: Single-locus perturbations of Calm1, Calm2, and Calm3 do not collapse onto a common basal neuronal calmodulin-loss transcriptional signature.

contributions.rationale: Anchors that Mib1 in L2/3 IT CTX Glut shows a restricted response including Pde4a, Ptprf, Rfx3, Gde1, and Fst, without a full ciliary proteostasis state.
Anchors that Ski's strongest unbiased positive neighbor was Mib1, sharing same-direction L2/3 up-regulation of Pde4a, Ptprf, and Rfx3.

higher_order_basis: Both findings identify the same L2/3 cortical cell group and the same-direction overlap of Pde4a, Ptprf, and Rfx3 between Mib1 and Ski, while bounding the interpretation away from a full cilia pathway or proven biochemical interaction.
scope: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut perturbation signatures for Mib1 and Ski; based on a small FDR-backed overlap and not a reconstructed ciliary pathway or biochemical-interaction claim.
statement: Mib1 and Ski perturbations converge on a restricted L2/3 cortical up-regulation module containing Pde4a, Ptprf, and Rfx3.

contributions.rationale: Adcy5 loss did not induce the same Scg2/Crem response, while Pde10a did, showing pathway-node specificity.
Drd4 did not converge with dopamine receptor or cAMP effector perturbations, extending the boundary against a broad dopamine/cAMP transcriptome.
Gnal and other source-arm nodes were flat where Pde10a activated Scg2 and Crem, narrowing the response to the degradation arm or basal state.
Gnas failed to phenocopy Gnal, Adcy5, Pde10a, and downstream cAMP-axis perturbations, supporting non-interchangeable cAMP wiring.
Pde10a loss produced the canonical compact Scg2/Crem-up response in 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA.

higher_order_basis: A positive Pde10a Scg2/Crem response is contrasted with flat or nonconvergent receptor, G-protein, adenylyl cyclase, and downstream cAMP perturbations.
scope: Dopamine/cAMP pathway perturbations measured by postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq, especially 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA.
statement: The detectable striatal-like cAMP transcriptional output in this assay is selectively elicited by Pde10a loss rather than by upstream dopamine receptor, G-protein, or adenylyl-cyclase perturbations.

contributions.rationale: Directly anchors that Rora was broad but mostly opposed to Bmal1 and that Rorb, Rorc, Ahr, Arnt, and Hif1a did not converge on the Bmal1 signature.
Qualifies the scope by placing the nonconvergent ROR/RORE relationship alongside a broader same-fold bHLH-PAS split rather than a universal transcription-factor detection failure.
Supports the claim by showing Rorc did not phenocopy measurable ROR/REV-ERB/circadian perturbations, especially where Rora and Nr1d1 were active.

higher_order_basis: The Rorc and Bmal1 findings jointly bound ROR/RORE and circadian relationships, showing that related circadian regulators are not interchangeable surrogates in the neuronal assay.
scope: Rora/Rorb/Rorc, REV-ERB/circadian, and Bmal1-related perturbations, especially in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut where noted.
statement: ROR/RORE-related perturbations do not reproduce the neuronal BMAL1-positive-limb loss signature, and Rorc itself remains nonconvergent with measurable ROR/REV-ERB/circadian perturbations.

contributions.rationale: Supports the buffering claim by showing Ndufa11 and 22 structural or assembly neighbors had near-zero same-pathway correlations and sparse downstream hits.
Directly states flat Ndufa12 behavior is shared across represented complex-I subunits and assembly factors.
Supports the class-level claim by showing 21 other Nduf targets did not converge with Ndufb10 into a generic complex-I transcriptional module.
Qualifies the claim as absence of recurrent nuclear transcriptional convergence, not a statement about enzymatic Complex I activity.
Directly states Ndufs4 belongs to a broader Complex I perturbation class dominated by on-target mRNA decreases with little downstream transcription.

higher_order_basis: Across several NDUF subunit or assembly-factor perturbations, the represented Complex I panel repeatedly shows sparse downstream DE and near-zero convergence, with caveats that respiratory-chain activity was not measured.
scope: represented nuclear-encoded Complex I subunit and assembly-factor perturbations in postnatal neuronal CRISPR/snRNA surfaces
statement: Represented Complex I perturbations in postnatal neurons are dominated by transcriptional buffering rather than a recurrent mitochondrial-stress nuclear mRNA module.

contributions.rationale: Anchors that Got2 produced only a weak, nonconvergent response in the matched thalamic group despite cytosolic Mdh1/Got1 ISR and synaptic-down signatures.
Directly anchors the absence of expected amino-acid/ISR, redox, p53, and MAS-compensation programs after Got2 loss across measured groups.
Supports assay sensitivity by noting that Mdh1/Got1 recovered a cytosolic-arm liability not reproduced by Got2.
Qualifies interpretation by emphasizing that transcriptomics cannot determine which metabolite changed and that AGC1 loss may be buffered or displaced from the assayed axis.

higher_order_basis: Got2-specific findings show expected severe-deficiency stress programs absent, while comparator findings demonstrate the same assay could detect ISR-like outputs after Mdh1/Got1 perturbation.
scope: Got2 perturbation across measured neuronal classes, especially 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
statement: Postnatal neuronal Got2 perturbation does not elicit the amino-acid/ISR, redox, p53, or MAS-compensation RNA programs expected from severe GOT2-deficiency models, despite those ISR-like outputs being detectable after cytosolic MAS perturbations in the same assay.

Supports adaptor-tier buffering by showing Sh3kbp1, Cblb, and Cd2ap were flat while Cltc generated broad differential expression.
Anchors the specific Cltc-versus-Synj1/Dnm1 contrast in matched groups, showing core clathrin perturbation reaches the nucleus while uncoating/dynamin perturbations do not.

higher_order_basis: All findings contrast broad transcriptional activity of core clathrin/endosomal nodes with flat adaptor, APP-linked, dynamin, and Synj1 perturbations.
scope: Neuronal transcriptomic responses for represented clathrin/endosomal and Alzheimer-risk trafficking perturbations
statement: Core clathrin/endosomal disruption is transcriptionally detectable in this neuronal screen, but CD2AP/CIN85-family adaptors, APP-linked targets, Dnm1, Synj1, Bin1, Sorl1, Psen1, and Abca7 do not form a shared clathrin/endosomal Alzheimer-risk transcriptional module.

contributions.rationale: Supports the proposition by including Kcnc1, Kcnc2, and Kcnc3 among neighbors that were flat or only singleton responders without a shared RNA module.
Anchors the Kv3-specific proposition by showing Kcnc1, Kcnc2, and Kcnc3 share absence of downstream transcriptomic responses despite self-transcript loss in some groups.

scope: represented Kv3 paralog perturbations in matched neuronal groups
statement: Represented Kv3 paralog perturbations lack a shared downstream FDR-significant transcriptional compensation program in postnatal neurons.

contributions.rationale: Directly states that CaMKII and calcineurin subunit perturbations fail to reproduce Calm3 anchor genes in matched responder groups.
Supports the broader CaM-adjacent nonconvergence by showing calmodulin, receptor, and PSD-95 perturbations differ from or lack the Camk2a RNA signature.

higher_order_basis: Calm3 and Ppp3ca signatures are not reproduced by canonical CaM effectors or NFAT/Ca2+ pathway comparators; CaMKII-family flatness bounds the interpretation to basal mRNA nonconvergence rather than signaling biochemistry.
scope: Calmodulin, calcineurin/NFAT, CaMKII, PKC, and IP3R comparator perturbations in steady-state postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq.
statement: Canonical Ca2+/calmodulin effector perturbations do not collapse onto a common steady-state neuronal transcriptional readout in this assay.

contributions.rationale: Qualifies the receptor-complex interpretation by showing Lingo1's Becn1 response was not reproduced by Lingo2, Rtn4r, Ngfr, or Trk-family perturbations, while noting biochemical interactions may still exist.

Anchors the reciprocal Trk-family boundary by showing Ntrk1 lacked same-family or data-driven convergent modules and had near-zero similarity to Ntrk2, Ntrk3, and Ngfr.
Anchors the neurotrophin-receptor claim by showing Ntrk1, Ntrk3, Ngfr, and Sort1 did not converge on the Ntrk2 response.

higher_order_basis: Trk, p75NTR/Sort1, and LINGO-related comparisons repeatedly show sparse, flat, or near-zero transcriptomic convergence, ruling out a generic neurotrophin-receptor transcriptional phenotype in this assay.
scope: Represented Trk-family, Ngfr/p75NTR, Sort1, and related receptor perturbations in postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq.
statement: Represented neurotrophin receptor perturbations do not produce a shared generic Trk/p75NTR transcriptional state in the measured postnatal neuronal nuclei.

contributions.rationale: Supports the broader innate-sensor claim by showing RNA-TLR and NF-kB/IFN comparators do not rescue a hidden Ifih1-like state.
Supports uncoupling of pathogen-sensor to IFN circuitry by showing TLR and IRF comparators are flat or idiosyncratic around Irf9.
Anchors lack of convergence among Tlr4, TLR-family, NF-kB/IRF pathway, and IL1R-related perturbations.
Anchors near-flatness and non-phenocopy across represented Toll-like receptor neighborhood perturbations.

higher_order_basis: TLR and pathogen-sensor contrasts independently show null, singleton, or near-zero-correlated surfaces rather than a basal innate receptor response.
scope: Represented Toll-like and RNA-sensing receptor perturbations in basal neuronal groups
statement: Innate receptor perturbations represented in the screen do not activate or phenocopy a basal neuronal PRR-to-NF-kB/IRF transcriptional program.

Anchors the biological scope by establishing that Klf7 loss produces a real but narrowly thalamic transcriptional response rather than a pan-neuronal phenotype.

scope: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut juvenile thalamic neurons in the postnatal transcriptomic perturbation assay.
statement: The juvenile thalamic Klf7-dependent transcriptional response is not reproduced by Fbxo38 loss in the same cell group.

contributions.rationale: Atp1a1 was buffered while Atp1a3 drove a distinct thalamic response, anchoring alpha-isoform specificity.
Atp1a2 did not phenocopy Atp1a1, Atp1a3, or Slc1a2, supporting separation of alpha2 astrocyte-associated biology from neuronal alpha3 biology.

Nkain2 was flat and did not phenocopy Na,K-ATPase alpha-subunit perturbations, especially the Atp1a3 thalamic response.

scope: Neuron-enriched perturbation screen of represented Na,K-ATPase alpha subunits and Nkain2, especially 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
statement: Na,K-ATPase-related perturbations are isoform-specific in neuronal nuclei, with Atp1a3 producing a distinct thalamic transcriptional response not reproduced by Atp1a1, Atp1a2, or Nkain2.

The upstream RAC1/CDC42-PAK-LIMK-cofilin pathway targets were nearly orthogonal to Cfl2 and lacked a shared DE module.
Kalrn perturbation produced no transcriptional feedback in Rac1/PAK/LIMK actin or measured PSD/NMDAR pathway genes, anchoring pathway buffering.

Tiam1 and expected Rac/EphB/PAK/WAVE neighbors lacked a recurrent FDR transcriptional module across many matched target-cell surfaces.

higher_order_basis: Across GEFs, small GTPases, PAKs, LIMK, cofilin, WRC, and related cytoskeletal regulators, findings repeatedly report flatness, near-zero correlations, or isolated single-gene events rather than a recurrent nuclear RNA module; caveats consistently limit the claim to transcriptome-level readout.
scope: Juvenile neuronal snRNA-seq perturbation screen across represented Rac/Cdc42/PAK/LIMK/cofilin and related actin-cytoskeleton pathway genes.
statement: The represented Rac/Cdc42-to-PAK/LIMK/cofilin actin pathway is transcriptionally buffered in juvenile neuronal nuclei, lacking a recurrent shared mRNA perturbation module.

contributions.rationale: Supports and qualifies the claim by extending the absent endocrine-axis readout to Lhx3 while emphasizing that endocrine pituitary cells were largely omitted.
Directly anchors the absence of a Pou1f1-dependent neuronal transcriptional response and absence of canonical pituitary hormone target movement.
Supports and bounds the proposition by showing the upstream PROP1/pituitary-output network is not induced in the same neuronal survey.

scope: Postnatal NeuN-enriched brain nuclei assayed after P16 mosaic perturbation, not anterior pituitary or Rathke's-pouch endocrine/progenitor cells.
statement: Acute postnatal neuronal perturbation of Pou1f1, Prop1, or Lhx3 does not engage a detectable anterior-pituitary hormone-cell transcriptional program in the sampled brain cell groups.

Anchors a compartmentalized Pde10a effect by showing its striatal Scg2/Crem response was not phenocopied by represented PDE, dopamine, G-protein, PKA, or Creb1 perturbations.

higher_order_basis: The Pde10a findings define a detectable striatal/LGE cAMP-linked output that is not reproduced by upstream receptor-to-cyclase source-arm or general cAMP-pathway perturbations.
scope: 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA and related basal postnatal neuronal readouts; missing striatal comparators and ligand-controlled acute signaling remain untested.
statement: In the striatal/LGE GABA group, the Pde10a Scg2/Crem response is a compartmentalized cyclic-nucleotide degradation-arm effect rather than a generic dopamine/cAMP pathway response.

contributions.rationale: Arid1a separated an Arid1a/Smarcc2/Smarce1-sensitive output from generic SWI/SNF dosage in the same thalamic group.
Bicra stayed flat where several BAF-family perturbations reported the thalamic module, separating ncBAF-specific BICRA from the active module.

statement: Tropomyosin and related actin-core perturbations in postmitotic neuronal nuclei do not induce a generic actin-damage or tropomyosin paralog-compensation mRNA program.
